Renders the system Apple Pay button. Only available on iOS.

Prop Type Required Description buttonType ApplePayButtonType Yes Button label type. buttonStyle ApplePayButtonStyle Yes Visual style. onPress () => void No Called when the user taps the button. disabled boolean No Ignores taps while true. See Disabled buttons. style ViewStyle No Layout/style (e.g. width, height). ApplePayButtonType: 'buy' | 'setUp' | 'book' | 'donate' | 'continue' | 'reload' | 'addMoney' | 'topUp' | 'order' | 'rent' | 'support' | 'contribute' | 'tip' ApplePayButtonStyle: 'white' | 'whiteOutline' | 'black'

import { ApplePayButton } from '@gmisoftware/react-native-pay' const handlePayment = async () => { // Call startPayment() from usePaymentCheckout here } <ApplePayButton buttonType="buy" buttonStyle="black" onPress={handlePayment} style={{ width: '100%', height: 48 }} />
Renders the Google Pay button. Only available on Android.

Prop Type Required Description buttonType GooglePayButtonType Yes Button label type. theme 'dark' | 'light' Yes Button theme. radius number No Corner radius in dp, like other React Native sizes. supportedNetworks string[] No The card networks your payment accepts, as in PaymentRequest.supportedNetworks. Default: visa, mastercard, amex, discover. googlePayAllowedAuthMethods string[] No As in PaymentRequest.googlePayAllowedAuthMethods. Default: both. merchantCapabilities string[] No As in PaymentRequest.merchantCapabilities. 'Debit' without 'Credit' leaves credit cards out. Default: every card type. onPress () => void No Called when the user taps the button. disabled boolean No Ignores taps while true. See Disabled buttons. style ViewStyle No Layout/style (e.g. width, height). The button can show the payer's card, so give it the same supportedNetworks, googlePayAllowedAuthMethods and merchantCapabilities as the payment, under the same names. Otherwise it may show a card the payment then refuses. With usePaymentCheckout, pass them from paymentRequest. An invalid value (an unknown network, auth method or merchant capability, an empty supportedNetworks or googlePayAllowedAuthMethods list, or no network Google Pay offers) logs a warning in development, with the same rules as the payment. The button then keeps the cards it showed before, or the default cards on the first render, and still calls the current onPress. An empty merchantCapabilities list is valid and accepts credit and debit cards. GooglePayButtonType: 'buy' | 'book' | 'checkout' | 'donate' | 'order' | 'pay' | 'subscribe' | 'plain' 'donate' is only for nonprofits that Google has validated. See The donate button.

import { GooglePayButton } from '@gmisoftware/react-native-pay' const handlePayment = async () => { // Call startPayment() from usePaymentCheckout here } <GooglePayButton buttonType="buy" theme="dark" radius={8} supportedNetworks={['visa', 'mastercard']} onPress={handlePayment} style={{ width: '100%', height: 48 }} />

With disabled, the button ignores taps, for example while a payment is in progress. It looks the same as an enabled button. Apple's Human Interface Guidelines ask you not to make the Apple Pay button appear unavailable, and Google's brand guidelines do not allow changing the Google Pay button's color. If the payment cannot start yet, for example before the payer picks a size, Apple suggests keeping the button enabled and explaining the problem after the tap. import { ApplePayButton, usePaymentCheckout } from '@gmisoftware/react-native-pay' function PayButton() { const { startPayment, isProcessing } = usePaymentCheckout({ merchantName: 'Your Store', currencyCode: 'USD', countryCode: 'US', }) return ( <ApplePayButton buttonType="buy" buttonStyle="black" onPress={startPayment} disabled={isProcessing} style={{ width: '100%', height: 48 }} /> ) }

Render one button per platform: import { Platform } from 'react-native' import { ApplePayButton, GooglePayButton } from '@gmisoftware/react-native-pay' const handlePayment = async () => { // Call startPayment() from usePaymentCheckout here } const style = { width: '100%', height: 48 } as const {Platform.OS === 'ios' ? ( <ApplePayButton buttonType="buy" buttonStyle="black" onPress={handlePayment} style={style} /> ) : ( <GooglePayButton buttonType="buy" theme="dark" onPress={handlePayment} style={style} /> )}

Low-level API for payment operations. Use it when you need full control over the payment request and do not want the cart/state from usePaymentCheckout.

import { HybridPaymentHandler, createPaymentRequest } from '@gmisoftware/react-native-pay' The native handler is created the first time you use HybridPaymentHandler, not when you import the package, so the package's helpers such as formatAmount and createPaymentRequest import on web and in Jest. Where the native module is missing (web, Expo Go, a build made before installing the package, or Jest without a mock), HybridPaymentHandler and getPaymentHandler() fail with an Error that says how to fix it: the Promise methods reject with it, and the others throw it. See Troubleshooting.

Resolves with whether the device supports the wallet and whether a card is ready. The check runs off the JS thread. import { HybridPaymentHandler } from '@gmisoftware/react-native-pay' const status = await HybridPaymentHandler.payServiceStatus({ supportedNetworks: ['visa', 'mastercard'], googlePayEnvironment: 'PRODUCTION', }) // status: { isSupported: boolean, hasActiveCard: boolean } isSupported — The device can pay with Apple Pay / Google Pay, whether or not a card is set up. hasActiveCard — The user has a card ready on one of supportedNetworks. Pass the supportedNetworks, merchantCapabilities, googlePayAllowedAuthMethods and googlePayEnvironment your payment request uses (PayServiceStatusOptions); hasActiveCard then counts only cards the payment accepts. Without them, both platforms ask about visa, mastercard, amex and discover. The Promise rejects with the configuration error that would fail startPayment for a value the payment would refuse: an unknown network, capability or auth method, or no network the platform offers. A check that fails for any other reason resolves both flags as false. Without googlePayEnvironment, Android asks the TEST environment, where hasActiveCard is true whether or not the user has a card. What each platform checks, and which button to show, is in Check availability.

Starts the native payment flow with the given request. Returns a promise that resolves with the payment result. startPayment validates the request with normalizePaymentRequest before it calls native code, as usePaymentCheckout does. An invalid amount (see PaymentAmount), a negative total, or a currencyCode or countryCode that isn't an upper-case ISO code resolves with { status: 'failed', code: 'CONFIGURATION', success: false, error }, and the sheet doesn't open. Call normalizePaymentRequest yourself if you want the error thrown earlier. import { HybridPaymentHandler } from '@gmisoftware/react-native-pay' const result = await HybridPaymentHandler.startPayment({ merchantName: 'Your Store', countryCode: 'US', currencyCode: 'USD', merchantCapabilities: ['3DS'], supportedNetworks: ['visa', 'mastercard', 'amex'], paymentItems: [{ label: 'Coffee Subscription', amount: '29.99', type: 'final' }], googlePayMerchantId: 'your_google_pay_merchant_id', }) // result: PaymentResult PaymentResult: interface PaymentResult extends PaymentDetails { status: 'success' | 'cancelled' | 'failed' code?: PaymentErrorCode // set when status isn't 'success' success: boolean // status === 'success' token?: PaymentToken error?: string // message for logs, also set on a cancel // From PaymentDetails, set only when requested: // billingContact, shippingContact, emailAddress, phoneNumber, shippingMethod } The promise resolves for every outcome, including a cancel and a misconfigured request; it doesn't reject. Branch on status and code. See Error codes for each code and PaymentResult for the fields. options.onAuthorize charges the token before the Apple Pay sheet closes. The result follows your callback: const result = await HybridPaymentHandler.startPayment(request, { onAuthorize: async (token) => { const charged = await chargeOnServer(token) return charged ? { status: 'success' } : { status: 'failure', error: 'Payment failed' } }, }) See Charge before the sheet closes for the timeout and Android behavior. On iOS, the merchant ID defaults to the first Merchant ID in the Info.plist key ReactNativePayApplePayMerchantIdentifiers, which the Expo plugin writes from merchantIdentifier (in a bare app, add it yourself: see Bare React Native). Use applePayMerchantIdentifier only when you need to override it at runtime. On iOS, the Apple Pay sheet lists your paymentItems and then a total labelled with merchantName ("Pay Your Store"). The library adds that total for you, so don't add your own "Total" item. Without merchantName, the total uses your app's display name. Build the request yourself or use createPaymentRequest for a single line item with defaults. Only one payment can be in flight at a time, on iOS and Android. A call made while another payment is still in progress, including one started by usePaymentCheckout, resolves immediately with { status: 'failed', code: 'IN_PROGRESS', success: false, error: 'A payment is already in progress' } and does not affect the payment in flight. A payment stays in flight until the native side settles it, right before its startPayment promise resolves. A new payment can start from that moment, even before your await continues. On iOS, the payment settles only after the Apple Pay sheet has closed. With onAuthorize, it also waits for your callback to settle or time out, so on iOS the payment ends once both have happened. Use isPaymentInProgress() to check first.

Synchronously returns whether a payment started with startPayment has not settled yet, including one started by usePaymentCheckout. While it returns true, startPayment resolves immediately with code: 'IN_PROGRESS'. import { HybridPaymentHandler } from '@gmisoftware/react-native-pay' const isBusy = HybridPaymentHandler.isPaymentInProgress() startPayment still checks for itself, so you can call it without checking first. The check is useful when you keep your own state around a payment and don't want to update it for a call that never starts one. usePaymentCheckout uses it this way.

iOS only. Opens Wallet (Settings on iPad) so the user can add a card. Call it from a Set up Apple Pay button (ApplePayButton with buttonType="setUp") when isSupported is true and hasActiveCard is false. It does nothing on devices without Apple Pay, and nothing on Android, where the Google Pay sheet lets the user add a card. import { HybridPaymentHandler } from '@gmisoftware/react-native-pay' HybridPaymentHandler.openPaymentSetup()

HybridPaymentHandler is a plain object that delegates to the package's single native PaymentHandler; it isn't a Nitro HybridObject. getPaymentHandler() returns that native object. Its startPayment skips the JS validation above, so pass it a request from normalizePaymentRequest. Both share one in-progress guard. import { getPaymentHandler } from '@gmisoftware/react-native-pay' const native = getPaymentHandler()

Custom checkout flow without the hook’s cart. One-off payments where you already have a full PaymentRequest. Flows that need full request control (for example shippingMethods, shippingType or a request built on your backend). Contact details such as shippingContactRequired work with both APIs; see Shipping and contact details. Need to check availability or supported networks without using usePaymentCheckout. For most apps, usePaymentCheckout is simpler: it builds the request from the cart and manages state.

TypeScript types exported from @gmisoftware/react-native-pay. Use them for request/result handling and server integration.

A monetary amount in the currency's major unit (dollars, not cents). type PaymentAmount = number | string Decimal string ('19.99'): exact. Must match ^-?\d+(\.\d+)?$; no exponents, spaces, or thousands separators. Number (19.99): read as the shortest decimal that round-trips, so 19.99 stays exactly 19.99. Results of float arithmetic such as 0.1 + 0.2 (0.30000000000000004) fail validation instead of being rounded. Before a payment starts, every amount is validated and sent to native code as a decimal string with the currency's number of decimal places (ISO 4217: 2 for USD, 0 for JPY, 3 for KWD). Native code converts it with NSDecimalNumber (iOS) and BigDecimal (Android), never through Double. A payment does not start when: an amount is not a finite number or a plain decimal string (NaN, Infinity, 'abc'); an amount has more decimal places than the currency allows (1.005 in USD, '1200.5' in JPY); the total of paymentItems is negative. Negative line items (discounts) are allowed. Google Pay accepts at most two decimal places, so on Android a three-decimal amount such as '1.234' KWD fails with an error.

A single line item (label, amount, type, and an optional kind). interface PaymentItem { label: string amount: PaymentAmount // number | string type: 'final' | 'pending' kind?: 'subtotal' | 'tax' | 'discount' // Android only } type is exported as PaymentItemType. final — Confirmed amount (e.g. product price, tax). pending — Estimate (e.g. shipping that may change). If any item is pending, the total is an estimate too: Google Pay receives totalPriceStatus: 'ESTIMATED' and Apple Pay marks the total summary item as .pending. Each item is sent to Google Pay as a display item with status set to FINAL or PENDING. kind is exported as PaymentItemKind. Google Pay receives it as the display item's type: 'subtotal' as SUBTOTAL, 'tax' as TAX and 'discount' as DISCOUNT. An item without kind is a LINE_ITEM, and the selected shipping method is a SHIPPING_OPTION. Give a discount a negative amount: kind only changes how Google Pay labels the line, not how it is added to the total. iOS ignores kind. Any other value throws before the payment starts. import type { PaymentItem } from '@gmisoftware/react-native-pay' const items: PaymentItem[] = [ { label: 'Coffee beans', amount: '18.00', type: 'final' }, { label: 'Coupon', amount: '-3.00', type: 'final', kind: 'discount' }, { label: 'VAT', amount: '3.45', type: 'final', kind: 'tax' }, ]

Full request passed to the native layer (or to HybridPaymentHandler.startPayment). interface PaymentRequest { applePayMerchantIdentifier?: string merchantName?: string totalLabel?: string // Google Pay total label, default 'Total' countryCode: string // ISO 3166-1 alpha-2, upper case: 'US' currencyCode: string // ISO 4217, upper case: 'USD' paymentItems: PaymentItem[] merchantCapabilities: string[] supportedNetworks: string[] shippingType?: string // ShippingType value, iOS only shippingMethods?: ShippingMethod[] // → PaymentResult.shippingMethod billingContactRequired?: boolean // → PaymentResult.billingContact shippingContactRequired?: boolean // → PaymentResult.shippingContact emailRequired?: boolean // → PaymentResult.emailAddress phoneNumberRequired?: boolean // → PaymentResult.phoneNumber // At most one: charges after today (see below) recurring?: RecurringPaymentRequest deferred?: DeferredPaymentRequest automaticReload?: AutomaticReloadPaymentRequest applePayMultiTokenContexts?: PaymentTokenContext[] // several merchants, iOS 16+ couponCode?: string // iOS only, needs onCouponCodeChange // Google Pay (Android) googlePayMerchantId?: string googlePayEnvironment?: 'TEST' | 'PRODUCTION' googlePayGateway?: string googlePayGatewayMerchantId?: string googlePayAllowedAuthMethods?: string[] // GooglePayAuthMethod values } On iOS, applePayMerchantIdentifier is optional. Without it, iOS uses the first Merchant ID in the Info.plist key ReactNativePayApplePayMerchantIdentifiers, which the Expo plugin writes from merchantIdentifier (in a bare app, add it yourself: see Bare React Native). Without googlePayEnvironment, Android uses 'TEST'. When it is omitted, an Android release build logs a warning once per app run from normalizePaymentRequest, which usePaymentCheckout, HybridPaymentHandler.startPayment and createPaymentRequest run before a payment. payServiceStatus, and the raw handler from getPaymentHandler(), log nothing. merchantName is the business name shown to the payer: the name on the Google Pay sheet and the label of the Apple Pay total. Apple Pay shows the last summary item as the total ("Pay label"), so on iOS the library appends a total item labelled with merchantName after your paymentItems, also when there is only one item. Don't add your own "Total" item. If merchantName is missing or blank, Android uses the app's label from the manifest and iOS uses the app's display name (CFBundleDisplayName, then CFBundleName). totalLabel labels the total in the Google Pay sheet, for example 'Razem' for a Polish sheet. It defaults to 'Total' and must not be blank. Android only: iOS labels the total with merchantName. Google Pay shows no total label for recurring, deferred and automaticReload payments, so it has no effect on them. merchantCapabilities takes MerchantCapability values. supportedNetworks takes PaymentNetwork names, matched ignoring case, and limits the cards the payer can choose on both platforms. A name that is not a PaymentNetwork fails the payment with code: 'CONFIGURATION' and an error that contains Unknown payment network "<value>". Use a PaymentNetwork value such as "visa" or "mastercard". A network the platform does not offer is left out, so one cross-platform list works: Android drops cartesBancaires, for example. The payment fails when no network is left. googlePayAllowedAuthMethods takes GooglePayAuthMethod values and defaults to both. Android only. billingContactRequired, shippingContactRequired, emailRequired and phoneNumberRequired ask the payer for contact details, which come back in the result as PaymentDetails. On Android, a phone number is collected with an address. See Shipping and contact details. shippingType takes a ShippingType value. shippingMethods takes ShippingMethod values; the selected one is added to the total. The first is selected by default on iOS and is always the one charged on Android. recurring, deferred and automaticReload set up charges after today and ask for a merchant token, which Apple Pay returns when the card's network offers one: see Recurring and later payments. paymentItems stay what the payer pays now, which may be nothing. applePayMultiTokenContexts pays several merchants with one sheet: see Several merchants. iOS only. couponCode is a code already applied, shown in the sheet's coupon field; paymentItems must already include its discount. It needs StartPaymentOptions.onCouponCodeChange, or the payment fails with code: 'CONFIGURATION'. iOS only; Android ignores it.

Returned from startPayment() (hook or handler). interface PaymentResult extends PaymentDetails { status: PaymentStatus // 'success' | 'cancelled' | 'failed' code?: PaymentErrorCode // set when status isn't 'success' success: boolean // status === 'success' token?: PaymentToken error?: string // message for logs, also set on a cancel // From PaymentDetails, set only when requested: // billingContact, shippingContact, emailAddress, phoneNumber, shippingMethod, // couponCode } type PaymentStatus = 'success' | 'cancelled' | 'failed' type PaymentErrorCode = | 'CANCELLED' | 'IN_PROGRESS' | 'CONFIGURATION' | 'NOT_AVAILABLE' | 'PROVIDER_ERROR' | 'UNKNOWN' status — 'cancelled' means the user closed the sheet before authorizing. It is not an error: usePaymentCheckout leaves error as null for it. code — Why the payment didn't succeed. 'CANCELLED' for a cancel, one of the others for a failure. See Error codes for what each one means and which native cases produce it. success — Kept for compatibility. Use status to tell a cancel from a failure. token — Set on success. Send it to your backend to complete the charge with your gateway, unless onAuthorize already did. Contact details and shipping method — A successful result also holds the ones the request asked for; see PaymentDetails. error — A message for logs, such as 'Payment cancelled by user'. Don't match on it; use code.

The error that usePaymentCheckout sets when a payment fails or can't start. It extends Error. class PaymentError extends Error { name: string // 'PaymentError' readonly code: PaymentErrorCode cause?: unknown // the error it wraps, if any } code — The same values as PaymentResult.code: 'CONFIGURATION' for an empty cart or an invalid request, 'UNKNOWN' when native code threw, and the result's code for a failed PaymentResult ('UNKNOWN' if it has none). A cancel and 'IN_PROGRESS' don't set error. cause — The validation error or the value native code threw. An empty cart and a failed PaymentResult have no cause. To branch in the handler that called startPayment(), read code from the result it returns. A failed result and error share the code, with two exceptions: a native result without a code keeps none while error.code is 'UNKNOWN', and 'IN_PROGRESS' leaves error as it was, often null. error is React state, so read it from the hook in the render after startPayment() settles, not from the value an event handler captured. The hook types it as Error | null; narrow it with instanceof PaymentError to read code: import { Text } from 'react-native' import { PaymentError, usePaymentCheckout, } from '@gmisoftware/react-native-pay' function CheckoutError() { const { error } = usePaymentCheckout({}) if (error instanceof PaymentError && error.code === 'CONFIGURATION') { // A bug in the app: log it, and show the user a generic message. return <Text>Payment is unavailable right now.</Text> } return error ? <Text>Payment failed. Try again.</Text> : null }

Optional second argument of HybridPaymentHandler.startPayment(). The hook takes these callbacks in its config instead. interface StartPaymentOptions { onAuthorize?: ( token: PaymentToken, details: PaymentDetails ) => Promise<PaymentAuthorizationResult> // Sheet callbacks, iOS only for now onShippingAddressChange?: ( address: PaymentSheetAddress, selection: PaymentSheetSelection ) => Promise<PaymentSheetUpdate> onShippingMethodChange?: ( method: ShippingMethod, selection: PaymentSheetSelection ) => Promise<PaymentSheetUpdate> onPaymentMethodChange?: ( card: PaymentSheetCard, selection: PaymentSheetSelection ) => Promise<PaymentSheetUpdate> onCouponCodeChange?: ( couponCode: string, selection: PaymentSheetSelection ) => Promise<PaymentSheetUpdate> } interface PaymentAuthorizationResult { status: 'success' | 'failure' error?: string // becomes PaymentResult.error, with code 'PROVIDER_ERROR', on failure } See Charge before the sheet closes for onAuthorize and Update the cart in the sheet for the sheet callbacks.

What the sheet callbacks of StartPaymentOptions get and return. iOS only for now; Android ignores the callbacks until #72. interface PaymentSheetUpdate { paymentItems?: PaymentItem[] // the new cart; left out = unchanged shippingMethods?: ShippingMethod[] // the new list; must not be empty error?: PaymentSheetError } interface PaymentSheetError { code: PaymentSheetErrorCode message: string // shown to the payer } type PaymentSheetErrorCode = | 'shippingAddressInvalid' | 'shippingAddressUnserviceable' | 'couponCodeInvalid' | 'couponCodeExpired' | 'other' // Redacted until the payer authorizes: no street, name, email or phone interface PaymentSheetAddress { countryCode: string // ISO 3166-1 alpha-2: 'US' administrativeArea?: string // state or province locality?: string // city postalCode?: string // only the start in the UK and Canada } interface PaymentSheetCard { network?: PaymentNetwork type: PaymentMethodType // 'credit', 'debit', 'prepaid', 'store' or 'unknown' displayName?: string // 'Visa 1234' } // What the payer chose so far, including the change the callback is called for interface PaymentSheetSelection { shippingAddress?: PaymentSheetAddress shippingMethod?: ShippingMethod card?: PaymentSheetCard couponCode?: string // the last code accepted without an error; in onCouponCodeChange, the code being checked } PaymentSheetUpdate — Return payment items only: the library adds the selected shipping method, later charges and the total, as for PaymentRequest. Amounts follow the same rules. When new shippingMethods still contain the selected one, it stays selected; otherwise the first one is. PaymentSheetError — The payer can't pay until they change what it refers to. On iOS an error from onShippingMethodChange isn't shown: Apple Pay has none for that change. Failures — Every sheet callback must settle within 25 seconds. If it rejects, times out or returns an invalid update, the sheet keeps its current items without an error. A rejection or an invalid update is logged in development.

The token you send to your server. Do not log or expose; treat as sensitive. interface PaymentToken { paymentMethod: PaymentMethod transactionIdentifier?: string paymentData: string // Opaque token payload (format depends on platform + gateway) } paymentMethod — Card/network and optional billing contact. transactionIdentifier — On iOS, Apple's identifier for the payment (PKPaymentToken.transactionIdentifier), generated on the device. Missing on Android: Google Pay doesn't return one. Key idempotency on your order ID instead. paymentData — Opaque payload for your gateway. iOS: Base64-encoded Apple Pay token data. Android: Google Pay tokenization payload (tokenizationData.token), gateway-dependent.

Describes the selected payment instrument. interface PaymentMethod { displayName?: string network?: PaymentNetwork type: PaymentMethodType secureElementPass?: PKSecureElementPass // iOS billingAddress?: CNContact // iOS } type PaymentMethodType = 'unknown' | 'debit' | 'credit' | 'prepaid' | 'store' PaymentMethodType is exported separately for direct typing. displayName — Describes the card to the payer, as the wallet words it: PKPaymentMethod.displayName on iOS, paymentMethodData.description on Android (for example "Visa •••• 1234"). Show it as is; don't parse it. network — The card's PaymentNetwork, or 'unknown' for a network the library cannot name. Use network rather than displayName for logic. type — How the card is funded: PKPaymentMethod.type on iOS, Google Pay's cardFundingSource on Android. Android reports 'credit', 'debit' or 'prepaid', and 'unknown' when Google Pay does not know; 'store' (a store card) is iOS only.

Card networks. Use these names in supportedNetworks; results report one of them in token.paymentMethod.network. type PaymentNetwork = | 'visa' | 'mastercard' | 'amex' | 'discover' | 'jcb' | 'maestro' | 'electron' | 'elo' | 'idcredit' | 'interac' | 'privateLabel' | 'cartesBancaires' | 'chinaUnionPay' | 'dankort' | 'eftpos' | 'girocard' | 'mada' | 'mir' | 'quicPay' | 'suica' | 'vPay' | 'waon' | 'nanaco' | 'bancontact' | 'postFinance' | 'pagoBancomat' | 'tmoney' | 'meeza' | 'napas' | 'bankAxept' | 'himyan' | 'jaywan' | 'myDebit' | 'unknown' // results only Platform Offers Google Pay visa, mastercard, amex, discover, jcb, interac, and electron, maestro and elo for Brazilian combo cards Apple Pay Every network but unknown. Some need a newer iOS: bancontact 16, postFinance 16.4, pagoBancomat and tmoney 17, meeza 17.4, napas and bankAxept 17.5, himyan and jaywan 18.4, myDebit 26 'unknown' is never a valid request value. A result reports it for a card on a network that is not listed here, instead of guessing.

Resolved by HybridPaymentHandler.payServiceStatus(). interface PayServiceStatus { isSupported: boolean // the device can pay with Apple Pay / Google Pay hasActiveCard: boolean // a card on the checked networks is ready } iOS Android isSupported PKPaymentAuthorizationViewController.canMakePayments() isReadyToPay hasActiveCard canMakePayments(usingNetworks:capabilities:) isReadyToPay with existingPaymentMethodRequired: true and the request's card parameters In the Google Pay TEST environment, hasActiveCard is true whether or not the user has a card. See Check availability.

What payServiceStatus checks. Pass the values your payment request uses, so hasActiveCard counts only cards the payment accepts. interface PayServiceStatusOptions { supportedNetworks?: string[] // default: ['visa', 'mastercard', 'amex', 'discover'] merchantCapabilities?: string[] // default: ['3DS'] googlePayAllowedAuthMethods?: string[] // Android only. Default: both googlePayEnvironment?: 'TEST' | 'PRODUCTION' // Android only. Default: 'TEST' } The values are checked as in startPayment, and the Promise rejects with the same configuration error for a value the payment would refuse.

Used in config and PaymentRequest for Android. type GooglePayEnvironment = 'TEST' | 'PRODUCTION' Use 'TEST' for development/sandbox; 'PRODUCTION' for live charges. Android uses 'TEST' when the value is omitted. See Testing payments.

How Google Pay may authenticate the card, used in googlePayAllowedAuthMethods (Android only). type GooglePayAuthMethod = 'PAN_ONLY' | 'CRYPTOGRAM_3DS' 'PAN_ONLY' — Cards saved to the payer's Google account. The token holds the card number and no 3-D Secure cryptogram, so Google requires you to run 3-D Secure (step-up authentication) for these payments as for any other card payment. See Card authentication and 3-D Secure. 'CRYPTOGRAM_3DS' — Cards tokenized on the device. The token holds a 3-D Secure cryptogram. Google Pay does not offer jcb or discover with it. The default is both. Pass ['CRYPTOGRAM_3DS'] when your gateway or Strong Customer Authentication requires device tokens. Android matches the values ignoring case, and any other value fails the payment with code: 'CONFIGURATION' and an error that contains Unknown Google Pay auth method "<value>". Use "PAN_ONLY" or "CRYPTOGRAM_3DS". They are separate from merchantCapabilities: every Apple Pay card is a device token, so iOS has nothing like 'PAN_ONLY'.

Merchant capabilities, used in merchantCapabilities. They come from Apple Pay; Android only reads 'Credit' and 'Debit'. type MerchantCapability = '3DS' | 'EMV' | 'Credit' | 'Debit' '3DS' and 'EMV' are Apple Pay payment protocols. PassKit needs at least one of them. EMV only covers China UnionPay, so every other card needs 3DS. Android ignores them. 'Credit' and 'Debit' limit the accepted card types. Both platforms match the values case-insensitively. Any other value fails the payment: the result has code: 'CONFIGURATION' and error: 'Unknown merchant capability "<value>". Use "3DS", "EMV", "Credit" or "Debit"'. iOS adds '3DS' when neither '3DS' nor 'EMV' is given, so [] is sent as 3DS and ['Credit'] as 3DS + Credit. Google Pay can leave credit cards out, but not debit cards: merchantCapabilities iOS accepts Android accepts ['3DS'] Every card type Every card type ['3DS', 'Debit'] Debit cards Every card type but credit cards ['3DS', 'Credit'] Credit cards Every card type ['3DS', 'Credit', 'Debit'] Credit and debit cards Every card type For 'Debit' without 'Credit', Android sends allowCreditCards: false to Google Pay, which UK gambling merchants must do. Prepaid cards stay allowed. To refuse debit cards on Android, check the card on your server before you charge it. Give GooglePayButton and payServiceStatus the same merchantCapabilities, so they are sent the same card types as the payment.

How Apple Pay labels the address, used in PaymentRequest.shippingType (iOS only; Android ignores the field). type ShippingType = 'shipping' | 'delivery' | 'storePickup' | 'servicePickup' For example, 'delivery' shows "Delivery Address" instead of "Shipping Address". Without shippingType, Apple Pay uses 'shipping'. Any other value fails the payment: the result has code: 'CONFIGURATION' and error: 'Unknown shipping type "<value>". Use "shipping", "delivery", "storePickup" or "servicePickup"'.

These iOS-only types appear in payment-related metadata returned by Apple Pay APIs (for example pass details tied to the selected card) and are mostly useful in advanced/native-integrated flows. type PassActivationState = | 'activated' | 'requiresActivation' | 'activating' | 'suspended' | 'deactivated' interface PKPass { passTypeIdentifier: string serialNumber: string organizationName?: string } interface PKSecureElementPass extends PKPass { primaryAccountIdentifier: string primaryAccountNumberSuffix: string deviceAccountIdentifier: string deviceAccountNumberSuffix: string passActivationState: PassActivationState devicePassIdentifier?: string pairedTerminalIdentifier?: string }

What the payer chose in the payment sheet besides the card, on both platforms. Each field is set only when the PaymentRequest asked for it. PaymentResult includes these fields, and onAuthorize receives them as its second argument. See Shipping and contact details. interface PaymentDetails { billingContact?: PaymentContact // billingContactRequired shippingContact?: PaymentContact // shippingContactRequired emailAddress?: string // emailRequired phoneNumber?: string // phoneNumberRequired, as the payer entered it shippingMethod?: ShippingMethod // the selected shipping method couponCode?: string // iOS, the last code onCouponCodeChange accepted }

Set at most one of these on PaymentRequest. Use them with HybridPaymentHandler.startPayment; see Subscriptions and later payments for examples and the validation rules. On Android they become Google Pay's Merchant Initiated Transactions; see On Android. // Shared by all three interface MerchantTokenPaymentRequest { description: string // what the payer agrees to; iOS only managementUrl: string // https, no query, fragment or trailing slash billingAgreement?: string // at most 300 characters tokenNotificationUrl?: string // where Apple tells your server the token changed } interface RecurringPaymentRequest extends MerchantTokenPaymentRequest { regularBilling: RecurringBillingItem trialBilling?: RecurringBillingItem // needs an endDate } interface DeferredPaymentRequest extends MerchantTokenPaymentRequest { deferredBilling: DeferredBillingItem freeCancellation?: FreeCancellation // iOS only } interface AutomaticReloadPaymentRequest extends MerchantTokenPaymentRequest { automaticReloadBilling: AutomaticReloadBillingItem } interface RecurringBillingItem { label: string // at most 100 characters amount: PaymentAmount // positive; a trial may be 0 intervalUnit: RecurringIntervalUnit // 'day' | 'month' | 'year' intervalCount?: number // positive integer, default 1 startDate?: Date // default: now, or the end of the trial endDate?: Date // default: no end } interface DeferredBillingItem { label: string amount: PaymentAmount // positive date: Date // when it is charged } interface AutomaticReloadBillingItem { label: string amount: PaymentAmount // charged on each reload; positive thresholdAmount: PaymentAmount // balance that triggers a reload; not negative } interface FreeCancellation { date: Date timeZone: string // IANA name, e.g. 'Europe/Warsaw' } There is no 'week' unit, because Apple Pay refuses it: use intervalUnit: 'day' with intervalCount: 7. Amounts are fixed; a price that depends on usage is not supported yet. Dates must be in the future. On iOS the sheet lists the later charges as their own lines, outside the total. Apple Pay needs iOS 16 for recurring and automaticReload and iOS 16.4 for deferred; on older versions the payment fails with code: 'NOT_AVAILABLE'.

PaymentRequest.applePayMultiTokenContexts takes one context per merchant, mapped to PassKit's PKPaymentTokenContext. See Paying several merchants for an example and the server side. interface PaymentTokenContext { merchantIdentifier: string // the merchant's Apple Pay merchant ID, or yours externalIdentifier: string // your stable ID for the merchant merchantName: string // shown in the sheet's summary merchantDomain?: string // e.g. 'hotel.example.com' amount: PaymentAmount // positive } The amounts must add up to exactly the total, paymentItems plus the shipping method, so list yourself too for any share you keep; all shippingMethods must then cost the same. A sheet update must keep that total, or the sheet keeps its items. The field can't be combined with recurring, deferred or automaticReload; such a request fails with code: 'CONFIGURATION' on every iOS version. Without them, Apple Pay needs iOS 16; on older versions the payment fails with code: 'NOT_AVAILABLE'. Android removes it without checking these rules. The result still holds one PaymentToken: each merchant's cryptogram is in its encrypted payment data, under authenticationResponses.

A delivery option in PaymentRequest.shippingMethods. See Shipping methods. interface ShippingMethod { identifier: string // unique within the request, returned in PaymentResult.shippingMethod label: string // e.g. 'Express' amount: PaymentAmount // added to the total while selected; must not be negative detail?: string // e.g. 'Next business day' } The selected method appears as its own line in the sheet and is included in the total. PaymentResult.shippingMethod is the selected entry as you sent it. On Android, Google Pay cannot offer a choice yet, so the first method is charged and returned.

A name and postal address the payer chose. Parts the payer left empty are omitted. interface PaymentContact { name?: string // full name, e.g. 'Jane Appleseed' givenName?: string // iOS only familyName?: string // iOS only postalAddress?: CNPostalAddress } In postalAddress, street joins the address lines with '\n', isoCountryCode is uppercase ISO 3166-1 alpha-2, and country (the country name) is iOS only.

CNPostalAddress is used by PaymentContact. The other types describe PaymentMethod.billingAddress, the card's billing contact on iOS. For a billing address on both platforms, use billingContactRequired and read PaymentResult.billingContact. type CNContactType = 'person' | 'organization' interface CNPhoneNumber { stringValue: string } interface CNPostalAddress { street?: string city?: string state?: string postalCode?: string country?: string isoCountryCode?: string } interface CNLabeledPhoneNumber { label?: string value: CNPhoneNumber } interface CNLabeledEmailAddress { label?: string value: string } interface CNLabeledPostalAddress { label?: string value: CNPostalAddress } interface CNContact { identifier: string contactType: CNContactType namePrefix: string givenName: string middleName: string familyName: string previousFamilyName: string nameSuffix: string nickname: string organizationName: string departmentName: string jobTitle: string phoneticGivenName: string phoneticMiddleName: string phoneticFamilyName: string phoneticOrganizationName?: string note: string imageDataAvailable?: boolean phoneNumbers: CNLabeledPhoneNumber[] emailAddresses: CNLabeledEmailAddress[] postalAddresses: CNLabeledPostalAddress[] }
type ApplePayStatus = PayServiceStatus
The main hook for payment checkout. It handles availability, cart state, and payment processing so you can focus on UI and sending the token to your server.
import { usePaymentCheckout } from '@gmisoftware/react-native-pay'

Pass a single config object. iOS reads the Apple Pay merchant ID from the native app configuration. Use applePayMerchantIdentifier only if you need to override it at runtime. Source of truth for these types: package/src/hooks/usePaymentCheckout.ts. interface UsePaymentCheckoutConfig { merchantName?: string // business name shown on the sheet totalLabel?: string // Google Pay total label, default: 'Total' countryCode?: string // default: 'US' currencyCode?: string // default: 'USD' supportedNetworks?: string[] // default: ['visa', 'mastercard', 'amex', 'discover'] merchantCapabilities?: MerchantCapability[] // default: ['3DS'] applePayMerchantIdentifier?: string // optional iOS override // Google Pay (Android) googlePayMerchantId?: string googlePayEnvironment?: 'TEST' | 'PRODUCTION' googlePayGateway?: string googlePayGatewayMerchantId?: string googlePayAllowedAuthMethods?: GooglePayAuthMethod[] // default: both // Contact details, returned in the result billingContactRequired?: boolean shippingContactRequired?: boolean emailRequired?: boolean phoneNumberRequired?: boolean couponCode?: string // iOS: a code already applied // Charge the token before the sheet closes onAuthorize?: ( token: PaymentToken, details: PaymentDetails ) => Promise<PaymentAuthorizationResult> // Update the cart in the sheet (iOS only for now) onShippingAddressChange?: StartPaymentOptions['onShippingAddressChange'] onShippingMethodChange?: StartPaymentOptions['onShippingMethodChange'] onPaymentMethodChange?: StartPaymentOptions['onPaymentMethodChange'] onCouponCodeChange?: StartPaymentOptions['onCouponCodeChange'] } merchantName — The business name shown to the payer. On iOS, Apple Pay labels the total with it, so the sheet reads "Pay merchantName". On Android, it is the merchant name on the Google Pay sheet. Without it, iOS uses your app's display name (CFBundleDisplayName) and Android uses the app's label. Set it on both platforms. totalLabel — Android only. The label of the total in the Google Pay sheet, such as 'Razem'. Defaults to 'Total'. iOS labels the total with merchantName. See PaymentRequest. supportedNetworks — The card networks the payer can choose, as PaymentNetwork names. Both platforms honour it. A network the platform does not offer is left out, and an unknown name fails the payment. Pass the same list to GooglePayButton. googlePayAllowedAuthMethods — Android only. Which Google Pay cards to accept: 'PAN_ONLY' (saved to the Google account), 'CRYPTOGRAM_3DS' (tokenized on the device), or both, the default. See GooglePayAuthMethod. merchantCapabilities — The card types to accept and, on iOS, the payment protocols. iOS adds '3DS' when neither '3DS' nor 'EMV' is given. On Android only 'Debit' without 'Credit' has an effect: it leaves credit cards out. Google Pay cannot leave debit cards out, so ['3DS', 'Credit'] accepts every card type on Android. An unknown value fails the payment on both platforms. Pass the same list to GooglePayButton. See MerchantCapability. supportedNetworks, merchantCapabilities, googlePayAllowedAuthMethods, googlePayEnvironment — Also used for the availability check, which fails like the payment for a value the payment would refuse. Set googlePayEnvironment: 'PRODUCTION' in a live app: in TEST, Google Pay reports a card whether or not there is one. Omitted, it is 'TEST', and an Android release build logs a warning once per app run when startPayment() builds a payment. The availability check alone logs nothing. billingContactRequired, shippingContactRequired, emailRequired, phoneNumberRequired — Ask the payer for a billing address, a shipping address, an email address or a phone number. They come back as result.billingContact, result.shippingContact, result.emailAddress and result.phoneNumber. See Shipping and contact details. onAuthorize — Called with the token and the requested contact details after the user authorizes the payment. Charge it on your server and resolve with { status: 'success' } or { status: 'failure', error }. See Charge before the sheet closes. An inline function is fine: startPayment() uses the one from the latest render, and a payment keeps that function until it settles, even if the config changes meanwhile. onShippingAddressChange, onShippingMethodChange, onPaymentMethodChange, onCouponCodeChange — Update the cart while the sheet is open, as in StartPaymentOptions. What they return changes only the sheet: items stays as you set it, so a coupon the payer tried and then cancelled leaves no discount behind. Inline functions are fine, as for onAuthorize. iOS only for now. See Update the cart in the sheet. couponCode — A coupon code already applied, shown in the sheet's coupon field. items must already include its discount. Needs onCouponCodeChange. iOS only.

interface UsePaymentCheckoutReturn { // Availability isSupported: boolean hasActiveCard: boolean isCheckingStatus: boolean refreshStatus: () => void // Cart items: PaymentItem[] total: number addItem: (label: string, amount: PaymentAmount, type?: 'final' | 'pending') => void addItems: (items: Array<{ label: string; amount: PaymentAmount; type?: 'final' | 'pending'; kind?: PaymentItemKind }>) => void removeItem: (index: number) => void updateItem: (index: number, updates: Partial<PaymentItem>) => void clearItems: () => void // Payment startPayment: () => Promise<PaymentResult> isProcessing: boolean result: PaymentResult | null // last result; check result.status error: Error | null // a PaymentError with a `code`; null after a cancel // Utilities reset: () => void paymentRequest: PaymentRequest } isSupported — The device can pay with Apple Pay / Google Pay, whether or not a card is set up. hasActiveCard — The user has a card ready on one of supportedNetworks. See PayServiceStatus for what each platform checks. isCheckingStatus — true until the availability check settles. The hook checks on mount and again when supportedNetworks, merchantCapabilities, googlePayAllowedAuthMethods or googlePayEnvironment change. The check never blocks the JS thread. refreshStatus() — Checks availability again, for example when the app returns from Wallet after openPaymentSetup(). isCheckingStatus is true until it settles, and the flags keep their last values meanwhile. Which button to show for each combination is in Check availability. items / total — Current cart and its exact decimal total, as a number (NaN if an amount is invalid). Amounts are number | string (PaymentAmount); use formatAmount(item.amount, currencyCode) to display them. startPayment() — Opens the native sheet. Returns Promise<PaymentResult> and never rejects, so check status and code (see Error codes). Except for 'IN_PROGRESS', it also sets result to what it returns, and sets error to a PaymentError with its code whenever status is 'failed' ('UNKNOWN' if a native result has none). Returns { status: 'failed', code: 'CONFIGURATION', success: false, error: 'Cart is empty' } when the cart is empty. Returns status: 'failed' and code: 'CONFIGURATION', without opening the sheet, when an amount is invalid or the total is negative (see PaymentAmount). error holds the validation message, and the validation error is in the hook's error.cause. HybridPaymentHandler returns the same result. Returns the native PaymentResult when the sheet closes. A cancel returns status: 'cancelled' and code: 'CANCELLED'. It sets result but leaves error as null, so the user closing the sheet doesn't show up as a failed payment. Any other failure from the native flow returns status: 'failed' with its code, and sets error with the same code and the result's message. A result without them gets code: 'UNKNOWN' and the message 'Payment failed'. Returns status: 'failed' and code: 'UNKNOWN' if an exception is thrown while starting/processing the payment, with the thrown message in error ('Payment processing failed' if it wasn't an Error). What was thrown is in the hook's error.cause. With onAuthorize, resolves after your callback settles. A 'failure' result becomes { status: 'failed', code: 'PROVIDER_ERROR', error } and sets error. Returns { status: 'failed', code: 'IN_PROGRESS', success: false, error: 'A payment is already in progress' } without opening a second sheet if a payment is still in flight, whether this hook, another usePaymentCheckout or HybridPaymentHandler started it. isProcessing, result and error stay as they were. This check comes first, so it also applies when the cart is empty. error — A PaymentError whenever it is set. Its code uses the error codes of PaymentResult and matches the failed result's code, except that a native result without a code gives 'UNKNOWN'. 'IN_PROGRESS' doesn't set it, so branch on the returned result. It is state: read it in the render after startPayment() settles, and narrow it with instanceof PaymentError to read code. paymentRequest / startPayment — Keep their identity until a config value or the cart changes. The hook compares the config by value (arrays such as supportedNetworks by content), so an inline config object is fine, and both are safe as hook dependencies and props of memoized components. reset() — Clears result and error (does not clear cart). It does not clear isProcessing while a payment is in flight; isProcessing becomes false when that payment settles. Call it after startPayment() resolves, once you no longer need result, so the token doesn't stay in the hook's state. Calling it inside onAuthorize is too early: the hook stores the result after the callback settles.

import { usePaymentCheckout } from '@gmisoftware/react-native-pay' const { isSupported, items, total, addItem, addItems, removeItem, startPayment, isProcessing, error, reset, } = usePaymentCheckout({ merchantName: 'Your Store', currencyCode: 'USD', countryCode: 'US', googlePayMerchantId: 'your_google_pay_merchant_id', googlePayEnvironment: 'TEST', googlePayGateway: 'stripe', googlePayGatewayMerchantId: 'your_stripe_merchant_id', }) // Single item addItem('Product', 29.99) // Multiple items; amounts can be numbers or decimal strings addItems([ { label: 'Product', amount: 29.99 }, { label: 'Shipping', amount: '5.00' }, { label: 'Tax', amount: 2.8, type: 'final', kind: 'tax' }, // TAX line on Google Pay ]) const result = await startPayment() if (result.status === 'success' && result.token) { // Send result.token to your server, then drop it from the hook's state. reset() } // 'cancelled': the user closed the sheet; `error` stays null. // 'failed': result.code says why. `error` is set too, except for 'IN_PROGRESS'.
If you call startPayment() when items.length === 0, it returns status: 'failed' with code: 'CONFIGURATION' and sets error to a “Cart is empty” error. Add at least one item before starting payment.

Use usePaymentCheckout when you want cart state + defaults managed in React state. Use HybridPaymentHandler when you need to build the full PaymentRequest yourself (for example shippingMethods, shippingType, subscriptions and later payments or prebuilt request payloads from your backend). The hook's total covers only the cart, so it doesn't take shippingMethods, recurring, deferred or automaticReload. Utility helpers for this path are documented in Utility functions.
Components (ApplePayButton / GooglePayButton) HybridPaymentHandler — Low-level API Types — PaymentItem, PaymentResult, PaymentRequest, etc.
Helpers for building payment requests, items, and formatting. All are exported from @gmisoftware/react-native-pay.

Use these functions when you are building a manual or low-level flow (usually with HybridPaymentHandler) and need to assemble PaymentRequest data yourself. If you use usePaymentCheckout, cart state and request building are handled for you internally, so these helpers are optional.

Builds a full PaymentRequest with one line item and sensible defaults. Required: amount, label. Defaults: countryCode: 'US', currencyCode: 'USD', supportedNetworks: [CommonNetworks], merchantCapabilities: ['3DS']. The amount is validated with normalizePaymentRequest, so createPaymentRequest throws for an invalid amount, and the returned request holds it as a decimal string. import { createPaymentRequest } from '@gmisoftware/react-native-pay' const request = createPaymentRequest({ amount: 29.99, // or '29.99' label: 'Coffee Subscription', merchantName: 'Your Store', countryCode: 'US', currencyCode: 'USD', // Optional: applePayMerchantIdentifier, googlePayMerchantId, // googlePayEnvironment, googlePayGateway, googlePayGatewayMerchantId, etc. }) // request.paymentItems is a single item: [{ label: 'Coffee Subscription', amount: '29.99', type: 'final' }] Use with HybridPaymentHandler.startPayment(request) for a manual flow.

Validates every amount in paymentItems and shippingMethods and returns a copy in which each amount is a decimal string with the currency's number of decimal places. See PaymentAmount for the rules. It also checks that currencyCode is an upper-case ISO 4217 code ('USD') and countryCode an upper-case ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code ('US'); 'usd' and 'USA' throw. createPaymentRequest, usePaymentCheckout and HybridPaymentHandler.startPayment already call it. Call it yourself to get the error thrown before the payment starts, or before passing a request to the raw handler from getPaymentHandler(). import { HybridPaymentHandler, normalizePaymentRequest } from '@gmisoftware/react-native-pay' const request = normalizePaymentRequest({ countryCode: 'US', currencyCode: 'USD', paymentItems: [ { label: 'Book', amount: 19.9, type: 'final' }, { label: 'Discount', amount: '-5', type: 'final' }, ], supportedNetworks: ['visa', 'mastercard'], merchantCapabilities: ['3DS'], }) // request.paymentItems amounts: '19.90', '-5.00' await HybridPaymentHandler.startPayment(request) normalizePaymentRequest({ ...request, paymentItems: [{ label: 'Fee', amount: 1.005, type: 'final' }] }) // throws: Amount for "Fee" has more than 2 decimal places, which USD allows, got 1.005 normalizePaymentRequest({ ...request, currencyCode: 'usd' }) // throws: currencyCode must be an upper-case code like "USD", got "usd"

Creates a single PaymentItem. import { createPaymentItem } from '@gmisoftware/react-native-pay' createPaymentItem('Subscription', 29.99, 'final') createPaymentItem('Shipping', '5.00', 'pending') // type defaults to 'final' The amount is stored as given and validated when the payment starts.

Sums the amount of all items with exact decimal arithmetic, the same as native code, and returns the sum as a number. Returns NaN if an amount is invalid. import { calculateTotal, createPaymentItem } from '@gmisoftware/react-native-pay' const items = [ createPaymentItem('Product', 29.99), createPaymentItem('Tax', '2.40'), ] calculateTotal(items) // 32.39 calculateTotal([createPaymentItem('A', 0.1), createPaymentItem('B', 0.2)]) // 0.3, not 0.30000000000000004

Formats a number or decimal string with the currency's number of decimal places (two when currencyCode is omitted), rounding half away from zero. Returns 'NaN' for an invalid amount. import { formatAmount } from '@gmisoftware/react-native-pay' formatAmount(29.9) // "29.90" formatAmount('100') // "100.00" formatAmount(1.005) // "1.01" formatAmount(1500, 'JPY') // "1500"
Parses a string to a number. import { parseAmount } from '@gmisoftware/react-native-pay' parseAmount('29.99') // 29.99 parseAmount('100') // 100

Returns whether network is in supportedNetworks (case-insensitive). import { isNetworkSupported } from '@gmisoftware/react-native-pay' isNetworkSupported('visa', ['visa', 'mastercard']) // true isNetworkSupported('AMEX', ['visa', 'amex']) // true isNetworkSupported('discover', ['visa', 'mastercard']) // false

Returns a human-readable name for a payment network. import { formatNetworkName } from '@gmisoftware/react-native-pay' formatNetworkName('visa') // "Visa" formatNetworkName('amex') // "American Express" formatNetworkName('mastercard') // "Mastercard" formatNetworkName('unknown') // "Unknown"

Constants for common network IDs (for building supportedNetworks): import { CommonNetworks } from '@gmisoftware/react-native-pay' CommonNetworks.VISA // 'visa' CommonNetworks.MASTERCARD // 'mastercard' CommonNetworks.AMEX // 'amex' CommonNetworks.DISCOVER // 'discover' Use with createPaymentRequest or when building a PaymentRequest by hand.
Supported versions and upgrade notes.

react — * (compatible with current React 18/19) react-native — * (0.70+ recommended) react-native-nitro-modules — >= 0.36.0 (required) expo — >= 53.0.0, optional (only if you use Expo; tested with SDK 57 / React Native 0.86). Package managers don't install it for bare React Native apps. Android minSdkVersion — 26+ (required for Nitro Modules prefab) Install the correct Nitro version first; the payment library depends on it.

iOS — the minimum iOS version your React Native version supports (min_ios_version_supported); visionOS 1.0+. Android — compileSdk and targetSdk 36, NDK 29.0.14206865, minSdk 26. To change them, set compileSdkVersion, targetSdkVersion, ndkVersion or minSdkVersion in the root project's ext block. When the root project doesn't define one, the library falls back to its NitroPay_* Gradle property, so a NitroPay_* property has no effect on a value the root ext already sets. Google Pay — the library depends on com.google.android.gms:play-services-wallet 20.0.0.
React Native 0.70 or newer (0.86 with Expo SDK 57) Expo 53–57 when using Expo

merchantIdentifier — Optional in the plugin config. If omitted, Apple Pay entitlements are not added (use for Android-only or when you add Apple Pay later). enableGooglePay — Optional. Set to true to enable Google Pay on Android, or false to remove the Google Pay manifest entry. If omitted, the plugin leaves the Android manifest as it is.

Platform Apple Pay Google Pay iOS Yes (ApplePayButton, usePaymentCheckout, HybridPaymentHandler) N/A (use Google Pay on Android) Android N/A Yes (GooglePayButton, usePaymentCheckout, HybridPaymentHandler) Use Platform.OS (or equivalent) to render the correct button and to pass platform-specific config (e.g. Google Pay options only on Android).

Regenerated Nitrogen bindings for react-native-nitro-modules 0.36+ (Expo SDK 57 / React Native 0.86). Peer dependency react-native-nitro-modules is now >= 0.36.0 (was >= 0.35.0). Example app upgraded to Expo SDK 57 (React Native 0.86, React 19.2.3).

Regenerated Nitrogen bindings for react-native-nitro-modules 0.35+ (JavaPart/CxxPart JNI model). Peer dependency react-native-nitro-modules is now >= 0.35.0 (was >= 0.31.4). Android minSdkVersion 26+ is required (Nitro Modules prefab). Set minSdkVersion to at least 26 in expo-build-properties or your app's build.gradle. Consumers on nitro 0.31.x must stay on 0.0.14 or upgrade nitro-modules first. Check the package changelog or GitHub releases for version-specific notes. When upgrading, run npx expo prebuild --clean and re-test on both platforms. If you use TypeScript, run bun run typecheck (or your typecheck script) after upgrading.

Do I need Expo? No. The library works in bare React Native too. The Expo plugin only simplifies adding Apple Pay entitlements and Google Pay metadata; in a bare project you configure those in Xcode and Android Studio yourself. Can I use only Apple Pay or only Google Pay? Yes. Omit enableGooglePay for iOS-only (false removes an entry another plugin added); omit plugin merchantIdentifier for Android-only. In code, only render the button for the platform you support. Which gateways are supported for Google Pay? Any gateway that supports the Google Pay API and the gateway token format. Commonly used: Stripe, Braintree, Square, Adyen, Authorize.net, Checkout.com. Set googlePayMerchantId, googlePayGateway, and googlePayGatewayMerchantId accordingly. Where do I report issues? GitHub Issues.
The repository includes a full example app in the example/ folder: an Expo app that demonstrates the checkout flow with usePaymentCheckout, cart management, and platform-specific buttons.

From example/app/(tabs)/index.tsx: import { Platform } from 'react-native' import { ApplePayButton, GooglePayButton, usePaymentCheckout, } from '@gmisoftware/react-native-pay' const { isSupported, isCheckingStatus, items, total, addItems, clearItems, startPayment, isProcessing, reset, } = usePaymentCheckout({ merchantName: 'Your Store', countryCode: 'US', currencyCode: 'USD', }) const handleAddCoffee = () => { clearItems() addItems([ { label: 'Coffee', amount: 4.99 }, { label: 'Tax', amount: 0.5 }, ]) } const handlePayment = async () => { const paymentResult = await startPayment() if (paymentResult.status === 'success') { reset() clearItems() } } {Platform.OS === 'ios' ? ( <ApplePayButton buttonType="buy" buttonStyle="black" onPress={handlePayment} style={{ width: '100%', height: 56 }} /> ) : ( <GooglePayButton buttonType="buy" theme="dark" radius={8} onPress={handlePayment} style={{ width: '100%', height: 56 }} /> )}

Checkout flow — Add items (e.g. “Coffee”, “Coffee Beans” with delivery), see cart and total, then pay with Apple Pay or Google Pay. Status — Check whether the device can make payments or only set up cards. Cart UI — Add/clear items and display total. Result handling — Success and error messages; reset and clear cart after success.
From the repo root: cd example bun install npx expo prebuild npx expo run:ios # or npx expo run:android

Use the checkout screen in the example app as a reference for: Calls usePaymentCheckout with countryCode, currencyCode, and optional platform-specific overrides. Shows a loading state while isCheckingStatus is true. Renders “Quick Add” buttons that call addItems or addItem. Displays the cart (items + total) and a “Clear” action. Renders ApplePayButton on iOS and GooglePayButton on Android with onPress={handlePayment}. On success, shows an alert and calls reset() and clearItems(). The Simulated Server toggle stands in for your backend's onAuthorize: in off mode no server charges the token, so the screen reports "Authorized (no server)", never a successful payment. Copy these patterns into your app: config setup, cart handling, and button usage.

documents.t: The example’s app.json includes the React Native Pay plugin (e.g. with a demo Merchant ID and Google Pay enabled). Change the plugin merchantIdentifier and any Google Pay runtime settings to your own for real payments.
Quick Start — Minimal integration in your app API: usePaymentCheckout — Hook options and return value Troubleshooting — Common integration issues and fixes

Decide which wallet button to show before the user taps anything. The library reports two flags, checked without blocking the JS thread: isSupported: the device can pay with Apple Pay or Google Pay, whether or not a card is set up. hasActiveCard: the user has a card ready on one of your supportedNetworks.

iOS Android isSupported PKPaymentAuthorizationViewController.canMakePayments(): hardware and parental controls allow Apple Pay isReadyToPay: Google Pay is available, and the user has a card or can add one hasActiveCard canMakePayments(usingNetworks:capabilities:) with your supportedNetworks and merchantCapabilities isReadyToPay with existingPaymentMethodRequired: true and your supportedNetworks, googlePayAllowedAuthMethods and merchantCapabilities Both flags are false when the check fails or, on Android, when Google Pay does not answer within 5 seconds. A value the payment would refuse rejects the payServiceStatus Promise with the configuration error that would fail startPayment: an unknown network, merchant capability or auth method, or a network list the platform offers none of (Google Pay has no idcredit or privateLabel). The hook logs the rejection and reports both flags as false.

On Android, the check goes to the Google Pay environment you pass as googlePayEnvironment, 'TEST' by default. In TEST, Google Pay answers hasActiveCard: true whether or not the user has a card (Google's reference), so a production app must pass 'PRODUCTION' to get real answers. An emulator with no Google account signed in answered false even in TEST, so test both signed-in and signed-out devices.
documents.s: Ask the environment you pay in

documents.t: Android: show the Google Pay button when isSupported is true. A user without a card adds one in the Google Pay sheet. Google offers no separate setup screen, so openPaymentSetup() does nothing on Android. iOS: show the Apple Pay buy button when hasActiveCard is true. When only isSupported is true, show the Set up Apple Pay button (buttonType="setUp") and call HybridPaymentHandler.openPaymentSetup() on tap. It opens Wallet (Settings on iPad) to add a card. Neither platform: when isSupported is false, hide the wallet buttons and offer another way to pay. In the example below, the checkout screen owns the hook and the cart, and WalletButton picks the button from the status. The user comes back from Wallet with a card the status does not know about yet, so the screen checks again when the app returns to the foreground: import { useEffect } from 'react' import { AppState, Button, Platform, View } from 'react-native' import { ApplePayButton, GooglePayButton, HybridPaymentHandler, usePaymentCheckout, type UsePaymentCheckoutReturn, } from '@gmisoftware/react-native-pay' export function CheckoutScreen() { const checkout = usePaymentCheckout({ merchantName: 'Your Store', supportedNetworks: ['visa', 'mastercard'], // The environment you pay in, so the status is real in production. googlePayEnvironment: 'PRODUCTION', googlePayMerchantId: 'your_google_pay_merchant_id', googlePayGateway: 'stripe', googlePayGatewayMerchantId: 'your_stripe_merchant_id', }) const { refreshStatus } = checkout useEffect(() => { const subscription = AppState.addEventListener('change', (state) => { if (state === 'active') refreshStatus() }) return () => subscription.remove() }, [refreshStatus]) return ( <View> <Button title="Add Coffee" onPress={() => checkout.addItem('Coffee', '4.99')} /> {checkout.items.length > 0 && <WalletButton checkout={checkout} />} </View> ) } function WalletButton({ checkout }: { checkout: UsePaymentCheckoutReturn }) { const { isSupported, hasActiveCard, startPayment } = checkout // `isSupported` is `false` until the first check settles, and a refresh // keeps the last answer, so the button does not flicker on return. if (!isSupported) return null if (Platform.OS === 'android') { return ( <GooglePayButton buttonType="buy" theme="dark" onPress={startPayment} /> ) } return hasActiveCard ? ( <ApplePayButton buttonType="buy" buttonStyle="black" onPress={startPayment} /> ) : ( <ApplePayButton buttonType="setUp" buttonStyle="black" onPress={() => HybridPaymentHandler.openPaymentSetup()} /> ) } The hook checks on mount, and again when supportedNetworks, merchantCapabilities or googlePayEnvironment change. isCheckingStatus is true while a check runs; the flags keep their last values until it settles.

HybridPaymentHandler.payServiceStatus() returns a Promise. Pass the same networks, capabilities and environment as your payment request: import { HybridPaymentHandler } from '@gmisoftware/react-native-pay' const { isSupported, hasActiveCard } = await HybridPaymentHandler.payServiceStatus({ supportedNetworks: ['visa', 'mastercard'], merchantCapabilities: ['3DS'], googlePayEnvironment: 'PRODUCTION', })
usePaymentCheckout: the hook's availability fields HybridPaymentHandler: payServiceStatus and openPaymentSetup Components: ApplePayButton and GooglePayButton
Ask the payer for an address, an email address or a phone number in the payment sheet, offer shipping methods, and read what they chose from the result.

Set any of these flags in the usePaymentCheckout config or in a PaymentRequest. Each flag fills one field of the result: Flag Result field iOS (Apple Pay) Android (Google Pay) billingContactRequired billingContact Billing name and postal address Full billing address of the card shippingContactRequired shippingContact Shipping name and postal address Full shipping address emailRequired emailAddress Email address Email address phoneNumberRequired phoneNumber Phone number Phone number, collected with an address (see below) A field is set only when you asked for it. Ask only for what you need to fulfil the order: each one is another step for the payer.

The details are in the result, and onAuthorize receives them as its second argument, so your server can check the address before it charges: import { useEffect } from 'react' import { usePaymentCheckout } from '@gmisoftware/react-native-pay' const order = { label: 'Coffee beans', total: '18.00' } // your order function useShippedOrder() { const { addItem, clearItems, startPayment } = usePaymentCheckout({ currencyCode: 'USD', shippingContactRequired: true, emailRequired: true, onAuthorize: async (token, { shippingContact, emailAddress }) => { const response = await fetch('https://api.yourserver.com/orders', { method: 'POST', headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' }, body: JSON.stringify({ token, shippingContact, emailAddress }), }) return response.ok ? { status: 'success' } : { status: 'failure', error: 'We cannot ship to this address' } }, }) useEffect(() => { addItem(order.label, order.total) return clearItems }, [addItem, clearItems]) return async () => { const result = await startPayment() if (result.status === 'success') { console.log('Shipping to', result.shippingContact?.postalAddress?.city) } } } With HybridPaymentHandler, set the same flags on the PaymentRequest; the details are in the PaymentResult and in startPayment(request, { onAuthorize }).

billingContact and shippingContact are PaymentContact objects: name: the full name, for example 'Jane Appleseed'. givenName, familyName: iOS only. Google Pay returns the name as one string. postalAddress: street (address lines joined with '\n'), city, state, postalCode, country (iOS only) and isoCountryCode (uppercase ISO 3166-1 alpha-2, such as 'US'). emailAddress and phoneNumber are plain strings. The phone number is in the format the payer entered. Parts the payer left empty are omitted, not empty strings.

Offer delivery options with shippingMethods. The hook doesn't take them, because its total only covers the cart, so build the request yourself and pass it to HybridPaymentHandler: import { HybridPaymentHandler, createPaymentRequest, } from '@gmisoftware/react-native-pay' async function payWithShipping() { const request = createPaymentRequest({ label: 'Coffee beans', amount: '18.00', currencyCode: 'USD', shippingContactRequired: true, shippingMethods: [ { identifier: 'standard', label: 'Standard', amount: '0.00', detail: '3–5 business days' }, { identifier: 'express', label: 'Express', amount: '7.50', detail: 'Next business day' }, ], }) const result = await HybridPaymentHandler.startPayment(request, { onAuthorize: async (token, { shippingMethod, shippingContact }) => { const response = await fetch('https://api.yourserver.com/orders', { method: 'POST', headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' }, // Your server prices the order from the method identifier, not the client's amount. body: JSON.stringify({ token, shipping: shippingMethod?.identifier, shippingContact }), }) return response.ok ? { status: 'success' } : { status: 'failure' } }, }) if (result.status === 'success') { console.log('Shipping with', result.shippingMethod?.label) } } The selected method is shown as its own line, labelled with its label, and included in the total. The total is your paymentItems plus the method's amount. The order matters. On iOS the first method is selected when the sheet opens, so put the default first. result.shippingMethod and the second argument of onAuthorize hold the selected entry of shippingMethods, as you sent it. Every identifier must be non-empty and unique, no amount may be negative, and the paymentItems must not total less than zero on their own: shipping can't make up for a larger discount. Otherwise the payment fails before the sheet opens, with code: 'CONFIGURATION' and an error such as Shipping method identifier "express" is used more than once. Android: Google Pay can't offer a choice yet (see below), so Android charges the first method: it appears as a line item, is included in the total and is returned as shippingMethod.

Phone number on Android: Google Pay only collects a phone number with an address. With shippingContactRequired, the phone number comes with the shipping address. Without it, Android asks for the phone number with the billing address, and asks for at least the billing name, country and postal code even when billingContactRequired is off. billingContact is still only set when you asked for it. Email and phone on iOS: Apple Pay returns them as part of the shipping contact, so the library requests them there. Without shippingContactRequired, no shipping address is requested. shippingType changes how Apple Pay labels the address, for example "Delivery Address" for 'delivery'. iOS only. See ShippingType.

Choosing a shipping method on Android: Google Pay only offers shipping options through its payment data callbacks, which the library doesn't use yet. Until it does, Android charges the first method. Prices or shipping methods that depend on the address on Android: on iOS, onShippingAddressChange updates the cart while the sheet is open (see Update the cart in the sheet). Android ignores it until Google Pay's payment data callbacks are supported. Limiting shipping countries on Android: on iOS, return a shippingAddressUnserviceable error from onShippingAddressChange. On Android, check the country on your server and resolve onAuthorize with 'failure'.
Use the cart API from usePaymentCheckout to add, update, and remove items before calling startPayment().

Single item: addItem('Product name', 29.99) addItem('Discount', -5, 'final') // negative for discounts Multiple items: addItems([ { label: 'Product', amount: 29.99 }, { label: 'Shipping', amount: 5 }, { label: 'Tax', amount: 2.8, type: 'final' }, ])
Change label or amount (or type) by index: updateItem(0, { label: 'Product (x2)', amount: 59.98 })
removeItem(index) // remove one item clearItems() // empty the cart

import { formatAmount, usePaymentCheckout } from '@gmisoftware/react-native-pay' const { addItem, clearItems, total } = usePaymentCheckout({ merchantName: 'Your Store', countryCode: 'US', currencyCode: 'USD', }) // Add product with quantity const handleAddProduct = (name: string, unitPrice: number, quantity: number) => { // 1.1 * 3 is 3.3000000000000003; round it to the currency's decimals addItem(`${name} (×${quantity})`, formatAmount(unitPrice * quantity)) } // Apply percentage discount (a negative line item) const handleApplyDiscount = (percent: number) => { addItem('Discount', formatAmount(-total * (percent / 100)), 'final') } // Clear cart const handleClearCart = () => { clearItems() }

At least one item is required before startPayment(). Otherwise it returns status: 'failed' with code: 'CONFIGURATION' and sets error. total is derived from items; you don’t set it manually. It is an exact decimal sum. Round computed amounts with formatAmount(value, currencyCode). startPayment() rejects amounts with more decimal places than the currency allows, which includes unrounded float results such as 1.1 * 3. See PaymentAmount. Discounts can be negative line items, as long as the total is not negative. Use type: 'final' for confirmed amounts (e.g. product price, tax); use 'pending' for estimates (e.g. shipping) if your flow supports it. One pending item makes the total an estimate. Google Pay shows the total as estimated (totalPriceStatus: 'ESTIMATED') and Apple Pay marks the total as pending. An estimate does not let you charge a different amount: Google Pay requires the amount you authorize and charge to match the totalPrice shown on the sheet, and a mismatch can be declined. If the final amount differs from the estimate, start a new payment with the final amount, unless your gateway explicitly supports adjusting it (for example, incremental authorization).

While the Apple Pay sheet is open, the payer can pick another shipping address, shipping method or card, and enter a coupon code. Pass callbacks to update the cart when they do: tax by region, an address you don't deliver to, a fee for credit cards, a discount code. They go in the usePaymentCheckout config or in the second argument of HybridPaymentHandler.startPayment(). iOS only for now. Android ignores these callbacks until Google Pay's payment data callbacks are supported (#72), so check the address in onAuthorize there. Google Pay has no coupon field. import { HybridPaymentHandler, type PaymentItem, type PaymentSheetSelection, } from '@gmisoftware/react-native-pay' // The whole cart from what the payer chose so far. Every callback calls it, // so the discount stays when the address changes. function cart(selection: PaymentSheetSelection): PaymentItem[] { const items: PaymentItem[] = [ { label: 'Sneakers', amount: '40.00', type: 'final' }, ] if (selection.couponCode === 'SAVE10') { items.push({ label: 'SAVE10', amount: '-4.00', type: 'final' }) } if (selection.shippingAddress?.administrativeArea === 'CA') { items.push({ label: 'Sales tax', amount: '2.61', type: 'final' }) } return items } export async function checkout() { return HybridPaymentHandler.startPayment( { merchantName: 'Your Store', countryCode: 'US', currencyCode: 'USD', merchantCapabilities: ['3DS'], supportedNetworks: ['visa', 'mastercard'], paymentItems: cart({}), shippingContactRequired: true, shippingMethods: [ { identifier: 'standard', label: 'Standard', amount: '0.00' }, { identifier: 'express', label: 'Express', amount: '9.00' }, ], }, { onShippingAddressChange: async (address, selection) => ({ paymentItems: cart(selection), ...(address.countryCode !== 'US' && { error: { code: 'shippingAddressUnserviceable', message: 'We only ship within the US.', }, }), }), onCouponCodeChange: async (code, selection) => code === '' || code === 'SAVE10' ? { paymentItems: cart(selection) } : { error: { code: 'couponCodeInvalid', message: 'Unknown code.' } }, } ) } One cart from selection. Each callback gets the change and a PaymentSheetSelection: the address, shipping method, card and accepted coupon code chosen so far, including this change. Compute the whole cart from it, as above, so one change doesn't undo another. Return payment items only. The library adds the selected shipping method, later charges and the total, as for PaymentRequest, and checks the amounts with the same rules. A field you leave out stays as it is. The address is redacted until the payer authorizes: country, state, city and postal code (only its start in the UK and Canada), without street, name, email or phone. onShippingAddressChange needs shippingContactRequired. The full address comes in onAuthorize. Shipping methods. Without onShippingMethodChange, the library adds the new method's amount to the current items. Return shippingMethods from any callback to change the list: the selected method stays selected while it is in the list, otherwise the first one is. An empty list is invalid. On iOS an error from onShippingMethodChange isn't shown, because Apple Pay has none for that change. The card comes as a PaymentSheetCard. Its type can be 'unknown' and its network missing, as with the simulator's card, so don't rely on them alone for a fee. Errors. An error keeps the payer from paying until they change what it refers to: shippingAddressInvalid, shippingAddressUnserviceable, couponCodeInvalid, couponCodeExpired or other. Its message is shown to them. Coupon codes. The coupon field appears only with onCouponCodeChange. A cleared field calls it with ''. Pass couponCode in the request for a code already applied. The last code accepted without an error is details.couponCode in onAuthorize and result.couponCode. Apple Pay doesn't put it in the token, so check the code again on your server and charge the discount for it there. Several merchants. With applePayMultiTokenContexts, PassKit needs the total to stay equal to the contexts' sum. An update may change the items and the shipping methods, but they must add up to the same total and every method must cost the same as before; otherwise the sheet keeps its items. An error alone always applies. 25 seconds. Each callback must settle within 25 seconds, like onAuthorize. If it rejects, times out or returns an invalid update, the sheet keeps its current items and shows no error; a rejection or an invalid update is logged in development. The hook's items don't change. With usePaymentCheckout, updates change only the sheet, so a coupon the payer tried and then cancelled leaves no discount in your cart.
