import { HybridPaymentHandler } from '@gmisoftware/react-native-pay' const status = await HybridPaymentHandler.payServiceStatus({ supportedNetworks: ['visa', 'mastercard', 'amex'], googlePayEnvironment: 'PRODUCTION', }) if (!status.isSupported) { // Hide the pay button and show "Apple Pay / Google Pay not available" } Pass the same networks and Google Pay environment as the payment request in step 2. On iOS, when isSupported is true but hasActiveCard is false, you can show a Set up Apple Pay button instead; see Check availability.

Either use a helper or build the object yourself: import { createPaymentRequest, HybridPaymentHandler } from '@gmisoftware/react-native-pay' const paymentRequest = createPaymentRequest({ amount: 99.99, label: 'Espresso Machine', merchantName: 'Your Store', countryCode: 'US', currencyCode: 'USD', googlePayMerchantId: 'your_google_pay_merchant_id', googlePayEnvironment: 'PRODUCTION', googlePayGateway: 'stripe', googlePayGatewayMerchantId: 'your_merchant_id', }) createPaymentRequest throws if the amount is invalid (see PaymentAmount). For multiple line items, build paymentItems yourself and pass the full PaymentRequest to startPayment, which applies the same checks with normalizePaymentRequest and resolves an invalid request with code: 'CONFIGURATION'. On iOS, the Merchant ID is read from the Info.plist key ReactNativePayApplePayMerchantIdentifiers, which the Expo plugin writes, unless you pass applePayMerchantIdentifier.

const handlePayment = async () => { try { const result = await HybridPaymentHandler.startPayment(paymentRequest) if (result.status === 'success' && result.token) { await sendTokenToServer(result.token, orderId) } else if (result.status === 'failed') { console.error('Payment failed:', result.code, result.error) } // 'cancelled': the user closed the sheet, nothing to report } catch (err) { console.error('Payment error:', err) } } To charge the token before the Apple Pay sheet closes, pass startPayment(paymentRequest, { onAuthorize }) and charge inside the callback instead of calling sendTokenToServer afterwards, so the token isn't charged twice. See Charge before the sheet closes.

Use the platform-specific button, and pass it status.isSupported from step 1 so it stays hidden when payments are unavailable: import { Platform } from 'react-native' import { ApplePayButton, GooglePayButton } from '@gmisoftware/react-native-pay' function PaymentButton({ isSupported, handlePayment, }: { isSupported: boolean handlePayment: () => Promise<void> }) { if (!isSupported) return null return Platform.OS === 'ios' ? ( <ApplePayButton buttonType="buy" buttonStyle="black" onPress={handlePayment} /> ) : ( <GooglePayButton buttonType="buy" theme="dark" onPress={handlePayment} /> ) }

One-off or fixed-amount payments (e.g. a single product, a tip). You already have a cart elsewhere and only need to build a PaymentRequest once. You want to avoid the hook’s internal state. For cart-based checkout, usePaymentCheckout is usually simpler.

Charge the payer again later, without them: a subscription, a hotel booking charged on arrival, or a balance topped up when it runs low. Set one of these fields on the PaymentRequest: Field For Apple Pay Google Pay Example recurring Subscriptions iOS 16 recurringTransactionInfo $9.99 a month after a free trial deferred One charge on a later date iOS 16.4 deferredTransactionInfo $240.00 on the day of arrival automaticReload Top-ups when a balance runs low iOS 16 automaticReloadTransactionInfo $25.00 whenever the balance drops below $5.00 The sheet shows the schedule and your management URL, and the payment asks Apple Pay for a merchant token instead of a device token. Your payment provider can charge a merchant token later, and it is not tied to the payer's device. Since iOS 26, the payer also sees the payment in Wallet under Preauthorized Payments. A merchant token is not guaranteed: when the card's network doesn't offer merchant tokens, Apple Pay returns a device token, as for a one-off payment. Ask your payment provider how it tells the two apart and which one it can charge later. These requests need HybridPaymentHandler.startPayment. usePaymentCheckout does not take them.

paymentItems are what the payer pays now. The later charges come from recurring, deferred or automaticReload, and the library adds them to the sheet as their own lines, outside the total. So the total can be zero: a free trial, or a booking without a deposit. When the first period is charged right away, put it in both places: in paymentItems for today, and in regularBilling for the schedule.

Google Pay calls these Merchant Initiated Transactions. The request sends recurringTransactionInfo, deferredTransactionInfo or automaticReloadTransactionInfo in place of the usual transactionInfo, and paymentItems with the first shipping method become its immediateTotalPrice and immediateDisplayItems. A recurring request sends only immediateTotalPrice. Google Pay doesn't allow regular charges in immediateDisplayItems, and a first period paid today is a payment item like a setup fee, so the sheet shows the amount due today without its lines. A free trial becomes an introductory period that ends on its endDate. Google Pay doesn't show the trial's interval, only its end. A paid trial is its own billing phase before regularBilling. description and freeCancellation are iOS only. With deferred or automaticReload, a pending payment item stays pending in the sheet, but these requests have no estimated total on Android. Google's guide mentions an early access program for Merchant Initiated Transactions. Check in the Google Pay & Wallet Console and with your gateway that your account can use them in PRODUCTION, and test the sheet in TEST first.

import { HybridPaymentHandler } from '@gmisoftware/react-native-pay' const DAY = 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000 export async function subscribe() { const trialEnd = new Date(Date.now() + 7 * DAY) const result = await HybridPaymentHandler.startPayment({ merchantName: 'Coffee Club', countryCode: 'US', currencyCode: 'USD', merchantCapabilities: ['3DS'], supportedNetworks: ['visa', 'mastercard', 'amex'], paymentItems: [], // nothing today recurring: { description: 'Coffee Club membership', managementUrl: 'https://example.com/account/membership', billingAgreement: 'Renews monthly until you cancel.', tokenNotificationUrl: 'https://api.example.com/apple-pay/tokens', trialBilling: { label: 'Free trial', amount: '0.00', intervalUnit: 'day', intervalCount: 7, endDate: trialEnd, }, regularBilling: { label: 'Coffee Club Monthly', amount: '9.99', intervalUnit: 'month', }, }, }) if (result.status === 'success') { // Send result.token to your server; your payment provider tells it // whether this is a merchant token it can charge later. } } regularBilling starts when the trial ends, unless you give it a startDate. Without a trial and a startDate, it starts now. intervalCount defaults to 1, so intervalUnit: 'month' is every month. There is no 'week' unit, because Apple Pay refuses it: for a weekly plan, use intervalUnit: 'day' with intervalCount: 7.

import { HybridPaymentHandler } from '@gmisoftware/react-native-pay' export async function bookRoom(arrival: Date, cancelUntil: Date) { return HybridPaymentHandler.startPayment({ merchantName: 'Seaside Hotel', countryCode: 'PL', currencyCode: 'PLN', merchantCapabilities: ['3DS'], supportedNetworks: ['visa', 'mastercard'], paymentItems: [], deferred: { description: 'Seaside Hotel, 2 nights', managementUrl: 'https://example.com/bookings', deferredBilling: { label: 'Room, 2 nights', amount: '960.00', date: arrival, }, // iOS shows it in the hotel's time zone. freeCancellation: { date: cancelUntil, timeZone: 'Europe/Warsaw' }, }, }) } freeCancellation is iOS only.

import { HybridPaymentHandler } from '@gmisoftware/react-native-pay' export async function enableTopUp() { return HybridPaymentHandler.startPayment({ merchantName: 'Coffee Card', countryCode: 'US', currencyCode: 'USD', merchantCapabilities: ['3DS'], supportedNetworks: ['visa', 'mastercard'], paymentItems: [{ label: 'Initial load', amount: '25.00', type: 'final' }], automaticReload: { description: 'Coffee card auto top-up', managementUrl: 'https://example.com/card', automaticReloadBilling: { label: 'Coffee Card Top-Up', amount: '25.00', thresholdAmount: '5.00', }, }, }) }

normalizePaymentRequest checks these before the sheet opens. How a broken rule surfaces depends on what you call: HybridPaymentHandler.startPayment resolves with status: 'failed' and code: 'CONFIGURATION', and the sheet doesn't open. normalizePaymentRequest and createPaymentRequest throw an Error. Call them in a try/catch. The rules are the stricter of Apple Pay's and Google Pay's, so a request that passes works on both, with one exception below: Set at most one of recurring, deferred and automaticReload. description must not be empty. managementUrl and tokenNotificationUrl must be https URLs without query, fragment or trailing slash. Wallet shows the management URL to every payer, so don't put account IDs in it. billingAgreement has at most 300 characters, each label at most 100. Dates must be valid and in the future. Build the request when the payer taps, not when the screen loads. A startDate must be before its endDate. A trial needs an endDate. regularBilling can't start before the trial ends, and without its own startDate it must end after the trial does. intervalCount must be a positive integer, at most 2,147,483,647. Amounts follow the currency's decimal places. The regular, deferred and reload amounts must be positive. A trial may be free (0), and thresholdAmount may be 0. One Google Pay limit isn't checked here: it accepts at most two decimal places, so on Android an amount such as '1.234' KWD fails with code: 'CONFIGURATION', as it does in a one-off payment. See PaymentAmount. On iOS older than 16 (16.4 for deferred), the payment fails with code: 'NOT_AVAILABLE' and no sheet. Offer another way to pay.

A merchant token only helps if your payment provider can charge it later: Check that your provider supports Apple Pay merchant tokens. Send it the token as for any Apple Pay payment. It returns a reusable payment method or a token ID, and you charge that on the schedule you showed. If the payment returned a device token instead, ask your provider whether it can still charge it later. Charge what you showed. The amounts, dates and interval in the sheet are what the payer agreed to. Charge a different amount or earlier, and the payer may dispute it. Handle token notifications. With tokenNotificationUrl, Apple, and Google as tokenUpdateUrl, tell that URL when the payer deletes the token or it changes, for example after a card replacement. Stop charging a deleted token. Let the payer cancel. managementUrl must lead to a page where they can change or cancel the plan. See Server-side processing for charging the token itself.

One Apple Pay sheet can pay several merchants at once: a marketplace order from several sellers, or a trip with a flight, a hotel and a car rental. Each merchant can then charge its own share. Set applePayMultiTokenContexts on the PaymentRequest, with one context per merchant. This maps to PassKit's multiTokenContexts. iOS only. Apple Pay needs iOS 16; on older versions the payment fails with code: 'NOT_AVAILABLE'. Android removes the field without checking it, because Google Pay has no equivalent: charge the merchants from your own server there. So test the rules below on iOS. Not together with recurring, deferred or automaticReload. Apple Pay refuses the combination, so the payment fails with code: 'CONFIGURATION'. Use HybridPaymentHandler.startPayment. usePaymentCheckout does not take this field.

import { HybridPaymentHandler } from '@gmisoftware/react-native-pay' export async function payForTrip() { const result = await HybridPaymentHandler.startPayment({ merchantName: 'Example Trips', countryCode: 'US', currencyCode: 'USD', merchantCapabilities: ['3DS'], supportedNetworks: ['visa', 'mastercard', 'amex'], paymentItems: [ { label: 'Flight', amount: '150.00', type: 'final' }, { label: 'Hotel, 2 nights', amount: '300.00', type: 'final' }, { label: 'Booking fee', amount: '10.00', type: 'final' }, ], applePayMultiTokenContexts: [ { merchantIdentifier: 'merchant.com.example.air-travel', externalIdentifier: 'air-travel', merchantName: 'Air Travel', merchantDomain: 'air-travel.example.com', amount: '150.00', }, { merchantIdentifier: 'merchant.com.example.hotel', externalIdentifier: 'hotel', merchantName: 'Seaside Hotel', merchantDomain: 'hotel.example.com', amount: '300.00', }, { // Your own share: the booking fee merchantIdentifier: 'merchant.com.example.trips', externalIdentifier: 'example-trips', merchantName: 'Example Trips', amount: '10.00', }, ], }) if (result.status === 'success') { // Send result.token to your server, as for any payment. } } The payer sees one total and authorizes it once. Apple describes a summary that lists each merchant with its amount; the iOS 26.5 simulator shows only the payment items, so check the sheet on a device. Field Meaning merchantIdentifier The merchant's own Apple Pay merchant identifier, if it has one. Otherwise, and for your own share, use yours. Your server tells the merchants apart by it, so see On your server before giving several contexts the same one. externalIdentifier Your stable ID for the merchant. Use the same one every time you request a payment for that merchant. merchantName Shown to the payer. merchantDomain Optional. The merchant's top-level domain. amount What this merchant may charge, in the request's currency. Must be positive.

The contexts must add up to exactly the total, so list yourself too for any share you keep, such as the booking fee above. Apple's documentation says they may add up to less, but PassKit refuses such a request with "The sum of all payment token context amounts must be equal to the PKPaymentRequest total" (seen on iOS 26.5), and the sheet doesn't open. So the library requires an exact total. The total is paymentItems plus the selected shipping method. Since the payer can pick another method in the sheet, every entry of shippingMethods must cost the same; the library can't tell which merchant a different shipping price belongs to. normalizePaymentRequest, which startPayment runs, checks both, and the payment fails with code: 'CONFIGURATION' when they don't hold.
documents.s: The amounts must add up to the total

documents.t: PaymentResult has the same shape as for any payment: one token. Apple Pay doesn't return a token per merchant to the app. The merchants' cryptograms are inside the token's encrypted payment data, and only your server can read them.

On iOS, token.paymentData is the base64 of Apple's payment token JSON: decode and parse it, then verify and decrypt it as for a one-off payment, following every step of Apple's Payment token format reference: check the signature and its certificate chain before you trust anything you decrypt. Or let a payment provider that does this handle the token. In a multi-merchant payment, the decrypted data has an authenticationResponses list, with one entry per context: Key Value merchantIdentifier "The submerchant identifier as provided by the coordinator merchant", in Apple's words: the context's merchantIdentifier. Confirm with your provider or a test token before you route on it. authenticationData The card network's cryptogram for this merchant transactionAmount The amount the payer authorized for this merchant Match each entry to its merchant by merchantIdentifier, and charge each merchant's share with its own cryptogram, for no more than its transactionAmount. Check the match against the contexts you stored with the order: exactly one entry per context, each with that context's amount. Entries can only be told apart by merchantIdentifier and amount, so when several contexts share an identifier (sellers without their own, listed under yours) and an amount, don't guess: refuse the payment, or ask your payment provider how it routes such entries. Ask your payment provider whether it supports Apple Pay multi-merchant payments and how it expects the token: many decrypt it for you and charge each merchant through their own accounts. The server-side processing guide applies as for any payment: look up the order and its amounts on the server. A provider that splits the payment in one operation can key idempotency on your order ID. If your server charges each merchant itself, one charge can succeed while another fails or times out. Then record each charge on its own, with an idempotency key per order and merchant (for example order_123:hotel), so a retry finishes the missing charges without repeating the ones that went through. When a charge's outcome is unknown, such as after a timeout or a server error, look it up with your provider before retrying, and retry with the same key within the provider's idempotency window.

When the user authorizes a payment, your app receives a token. Nothing has been charged yet: your backend must use this token with your payment gateway (Stripe, Braintree, etc.) to create the charge. Send it from onAuthorize, so the payment sheet shows your server's answer.

From the client, send at least: token — The full PaymentToken object (or the fields your gateway needs). Treat as sensitive. Once it is sent, drop it: with usePaymentCheckout, call reset() after startPayment() resolves, also when onAuthorize sent the token, since the hook stores the result only then. Don't put the result or token in navigation params or a global store. order/cart id — So the server knows what was purchased, and as the base of your idempotency key. Don't send the amount to charge. The server looks up the order and charges the amount and currency it stored. If you also send the total the user saw, the server only compares it with the order and rejects a mismatch. Don't key idempotency on token.transactionIdentifier: it is missing on Android. The simplest flow sends the token after startPayment() resolves. On iOS the sheet has already shown success by then, so don't tell the user the payment succeeded until your server answers, or use onAuthorize instead: import { useEffect } from 'react' import { usePaymentCheckout } from '@gmisoftware/react-native-pay' const order = { id: 'order_123', label: 'Premium plan', total: '49.99' } // your order function useOrderPayment() { const { addItem, clearItems, startPayment, reset } = usePaymentCheckout({ currencyCode: 'USD', }) // Fill the cart before the user taps pay: startPayment() fails for an // empty cart, and items added in the same handler arrive too late. useEffect(() => { addItem(order.label, order.total) return clearItems }, [addItem, clearItems]) // Pass this to the pay button's onPress. return async () => { const result = await startPayment() if (result.status === 'success' && result.token) { // Drop the token from the hook's state before the request, so a later // payment's result can't be cleared by this one. reset() const response = await fetch('https://api.yourserver.com/process-payment', { method: 'POST', headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' }, body: JSON.stringify({ token: result.token, orderId: order.id }), }) if (!response.ok) throw new Error('Payment processing failed') } } }
documents.s: What to send to the server

documents.t: Without onAuthorize, Apple Pay shows its success checkmark as soon as the user authorizes, before your server has charged anything. If the charge then fails, the user has already seen "Done". Pass onAuthorize to charge the token while the sheet waits. Resolve with the outcome, and the sheet shows success or failure: import { useEffect } from 'react' import { usePaymentCheckout } from '@gmisoftware/react-native-pay' const order = { id: 'order_123', label: 'Premium plan', total: '49.99' } // your order function useOrderPayment() { const { addItem, clearItems, startPayment, reset } = usePaymentCheckout({ currencyCode: 'USD', onAuthorize: async (token) => { const response = await fetch('https://api.yourserver.com/process-payment', { method: 'POST', headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' }, body: JSON.stringify({ token, orderId: order.id }), }) if (!response.ok) { const { error } = await response.json() return { status: 'failure', error } } return { status: 'success' } }, }) useEffect(() => { addItem(order.label, order.total) return clearItems }, [addItem, clearItems]) return async () => { const result = await startPayment() // result.status is 'success' only when onAuthorize returned 'success'. // The token is already charged, so don't send it to your server again. // The hook stored the result only now, so drop the token here. if (result.status === 'success') reset() } } With HybridPaymentHandler, pass the same callback as startPayment(request, { onAuthorize }). The second argument of onAuthorize holds the contact details and shipping method the request asked for, such as the shipping address. See Shipping and contact details. How it behaves: Failure: { status: 'failure', error } makes the sheet show the failure state. startPayment resolves with status: 'failed', code: 'PROVIDER_ERROR' and your error. A rejected promise is treated the same way. Retries on iOS: if the user retries from the sheet after a failure or a timeout, onAuthorize runs again with the new token. The result reflects the last attempt. A retry can start while a timed-out charge is still running, so key idempotency on your order ID, not on the token. Timeout: onAuthorize must settle within 25 seconds (Apple Pay itself gives up after about 30). Otherwise the payment fails with code: 'PROVIDER_ERROR' and "Payment authorization timed out", and the late result is ignored. Your server may still have charged the card, so make the charge idempotent and reconcile by order ID. Android: Google Pay closes its sheet before it returns the token, and its basic flow has no step that waits for the merchant. onAuthorize still runs, with the same timeout, after the sheet closes, and its outcome decides the PaymentResult. The same callback works on both platforms.

Your backend receives the token and calls your gateway SDK/API. The exact request body and field mapping depend on your gateway + tokenization mode. Treat this example as shape guidance, not drop-in code. // Backend (Node.js example) app.post('/process-payment', async (req, res) => { // Never read the amount to charge from the request body. `total` is only // the amount the sheet showed, to compare with the order. const { token, orderId, total } = req.body try { // 1) Load the order server-side and check that it belongs to this user // and is still unpaid. // 2) Choose gateway flow based on platform/gateway config // - iOS (Apple Pay): paymentData is Apple token payload (Base64 string) // - Android (Google Pay): paymentData is Google tokenization payload // 3) Call gateway API with the exact fields required by that provider // 4) Use idempotency keys and persist payment state const order = await orders.findForUser(orderId, req.user.id) if (!order) return res.status(404).json({ error: 'Order not found' }) if (order.status === 'paid') return res.json({ success: true, chargeId: order.chargeId }) // The order changed after the app showed it: don't charge an amount the // user didn't see. `order.total` is the decimal string, such as '49.99'. if (total !== undefined && total !== order.total) { return res.status(409).json({ error: 'The order total has changed' }) } const charge = await gateway.charge({ // Store totals in the currency's minor unit: 2 decimals for USD, // 0 for JPY, 3 for KWD. Don't multiply a decimal amount by 100. amountMinor: order.totalMinor, currency: order.currency, tokenPayload: token.paymentData, token: token, orderId: order.id, idempotencyKey: `charge-${order.id}`, }) // Report success only for a completed charge. A decline or a pending // charge must not show success in the app. Use your gateway's status value. if (charge.status !== 'succeeded') { return res.status(402).json({ error: 'The payment was not completed' }) } res.json({ success: true, chargeId: charge.id }) } catch (err) { res.status(500).json({ error: err.message }) } }) Important: Use your gateway’s official docs for: Mapping PaymentToken fields to provider-specific request fields. Creating a payment method/source/intent from Apple Pay or Google Pay token payloads. Idempotency (e.g. a key derived from your order ID to avoid duplicate charges). Handling failures and refunds. Provider-specific walkthroughs in Przelewy24 Apple Pay + Google Pay cookbook.

Use HTTPS and authenticate the client (e.g. session or API key). Take the amount and currency from the server-side order; never charge an amount the client sent. Do not log raw token payloads; treat them like card data. Prefer creating a PaymentIntent (or equivalent) on the server and confirming with the token, so the server controls the amount and idempotency.

Before you release, run a payment end to end on both platforms: in the Apple Pay sandbox on an iPhone, and in the Google Pay TEST environment on Android. This page covers both setups, the production access Google requires, and the flows to check before every release.

Only PRODUCTION with real cards proves that a charge goes through. Each test environment covers part of the flow: Environment Verifies Cannot verify iOS Simulator The sheet opens and shows your line items and the "Pay merchantName" total. Cancel, onAuthorize success and failure, and the double-tap guard. No card or account needed. A token your gateway can charge. Apple doesn't document what the Simulator's token contains, and developers report that its paymentData is empty. Apple also says the Simulator doesn't support every Apple Pay feature, without listing which. iPhone with a sandbox tester The full sheet with Apple's test cards, Face ID or passcode, and a token your payment processor can test decrypting. A completed charge. Apple says sandbox transactions are declined before fulfillment, because the test key doesn't match your production key. Android, TEST environment The Google Pay sheet with Google's test cards, the result handling, and onAuthorize. No Google Pay merchant ID needed. Availability: hasActiveCard is always true in TEST. A live charge: TEST tokens never carry real card data, so only your gateway's test environment can process them. Your production request: the merchant ID and the PRODUCTION checks only run in PRODUCTION. Android, PRODUCTION Everything, with real cards. Nothing. It needs production access first. Availability is hard to test on both platforms. On iOS, isSupported comes from PKPaymentAuthorizationViewController.canMakePayments(), which Apple documents as true when the device supports payments, even with no card in Wallet; hasActiveCard also needs a card on your networks. On Android, both flags come from the environment you pass as googlePayEnvironment, so only a PRODUCTION build shows real answers. See Check availability.

The Simulator runs the Apple Pay sheet without a card in Wallet or a sandbox account: npx expo run:ios Use it to check the sheet's contents and your app's handling of each result (see the release checklist). Don't send the Simulator's token to your gateway, and test anything that depends on a real token, such as your server's charge, on a device.

Apple's sandbox testing page lists the supported regions and the test card numbers. To run a sandbox payment: Create a sandbox tester. In App Store Connect, open Users and Access, then Sandbox, then Testers, and click +. Use an email address that isn't already an Apple Account. Sign the device in as the tester. On the iPhone, sign out of your Apple Account in Settings, then sign in with the sandbox tester. For Apple Pay the tester must be the device's Apple Account, not only the App Store's sandbox account. Set a supported region. In Settings → General → Language & Region, pick a region where Apple Pay sandbox is supported. Amex test cards only work with the UK or US region. Add a test card. In Wallet, tap +, choose a debit or credit card, and enter one of Apple's test cards manually. If Wallet asks for a verification code, enter 111111. Install a development build with Developer Mode on: npx expo run:ios --device The Merchant ID in your plugin config must belong to your Apple Developer team. The example app's Merchant ID (merchant.pl.sfd.sklep) won't sign with yours, so replace it before you run the example on a device. Pay. The sheet shows your test card. After you authorize, startPayment resolves with a sandbox token. What you do with the sandbox token depends on your gateway. Apple says your processor can use it to test decrypting the payment data, but the charge itself is declined. Some gateways don't take sandbox tokens at all: Stripe, for example, asks you to test with a real card in Wallet and its test API keys, and doesn't charge the card. Check your gateway's Apple Pay docs. Test cards only work in the sandbox, and real cards only work in production. Before release, sign the device back in to a regular Apple Account and pay once with a real card. If your gateway has a test mode for real cards, use it. If not, make a small charge and refund it.

Android uses the TEST environment unless you set googlePayEnvironment: 'PRODUCTION'. You need: A real device, or an emulator with a Google Play system image, signed in to a Google account. Google Wallet with a payment method. Google's setup page asks you to add one. Then run a development build: npx expo run:android In TEST, Google Pay shows a suite of test cards by default. You don't need to join anything. To see your account's real cards in TEST instead, join the googlepay-test-mode-real-data group. Real cards return placeholder data in TEST and are never charged. In TEST, the sheet always labels you as an unverified merchant. Get a token your gateway accepts. If you leave googlePayGateway and googlePayGatewayMerchantId empty in TEST, the library sends Google's example gateway with exampleGatewayMerchantId. Google says the example gateway returns no card data capable of a transaction, so your server can't charge it. To send a token to your gateway's test environment, set its test values: import { usePaymentCheckout } from '@gmisoftware/react-native-pay' usePaymentCheckout({ googlePayEnvironment: 'TEST', googlePayGateway: 'your_gateway', googlePayGatewayMerchantId: 'your_test_gateway_merchant_id', }) Some gateways, such as Stripe, Braintree, and Adyen, show their own test cards in the sheet when the request carries their test parameters, and their test environment returns realistic responses. The library sends only gateway and gatewayMerchantId as tokenization parameters, so check your gateway's entry for the parameters it expects. What TEST can't verify: Availability. With existingPaymentMethodRequired, isReadyToPay always returns true in TEST, so hasActiveCard is true even with no card. An emulator with no Google account signed in answers false instead. You can't test the "no card" path of a signed-in user in TEST. A live charge. TEST tokens never carry real card data. With your gateway's test values, its test environment can process them, but nothing is charged. Your production request. The library sends googlePayMerchantId and requires googlePayMerchantId, googlePayGateway, and googlePayGatewayMerchantId only in PRODUCTION. A missing value fails with, for example, googlePayMerchantId is required in PRODUCTION, which you only see in a PRODUCTION build.

Google Pay only works in PRODUCTION after Google approves your app. Google's publishing guide has the full steps. In short: In the Google Pay & Wallet Console, choose the Merchant business type and complete your business profile. Open Google Pay API, then Get started, and accept the Google Pay API Terms of Service and Acceptable Use Policy. Your Google Pay merchant ID then appears in the Console. Pass it as googlePayMerchantId. Go through the integration checklist against your TEST build. Under Google Pay API → Integrations → Integrate with your Android app, pick your app and the Gateway integration type. The Console only lists apps published on Google Play under the same Google account. Upload screenshots of your TEST integration, and submit the app for approval. Once approved, set googlePayEnvironment: 'PRODUCTION' and your production gateway values, sign the app with your release key, and publish it on Google Play. Google says the debug key doesn't work in PRODUCTION. Until your app has production access, the sheet shows an "Unrecognized App" error. To find out why a PRODUCTION request fails, read the merchant error log: adb logcat -s WalletMerchantError Google's troubleshooting page lists the error codes, such as OR_BIBED_06 for the example gateway in production, and OR_BIBED_13 for a signing key that doesn't match.

Run these flows on an iPhone and on an Android device before every release, with the build configuration you ship. The example app's Simulated Server (onAuthorize) button rehearses them without a backend: tap it to cycle between off, approve, and decline. In approve and decline it waits 1.5 seconds and then resolves like a server that charged or declined the token. In your own app, use your server against your gateway's test mode, and your gateway's decline test cards or amounts for the decline flow. Success. Pay with a test card. startPayment resolves with status: 'success' and a token, and your server charges once. With onAuthorize, the Apple Pay sheet shows its checkmark only after your server answers. On Android, the Google Pay sheet closes first and onAuthorize runs after. User cancel. Open the sheet and close it without paying. startPayment resolves with status: 'cancelled' and code: 'CANCELLED'. Your server is not called. The hook leaves error as null, so your UI shows no failure. Decline through onAuthorize. Set the example app to decline, or make your server decline. On iOS, the sheet shows the failure and lets the user retry, which calls onAuthorize again with a new token. Closing the sheet resolves startPayment with status: 'failed', code: 'PROVIDER_ERROR' and your error. On Android, the sheet has already closed, and startPayment resolves with status: 'failed', code: 'PROVIDER_ERROR' and your error. The order isn't marked paid, and a retry doesn't charge twice. Make the charge idempotent per order ID, not per token. Slow server. Make your server take longer than 25 seconds to answer onAuthorize. startPayment resolves with code: 'PROVIDER_ERROR' and error: 'Payment authorization timed out'. On iOS, the user can first retry from the sheet. Your server may still charge after the app has given up. Check that your backend can reconcile that order. Double tap. Tap the pay button twice quickly. Only one sheet opens. The second call resolves at once with code: 'IN_PROGRESS', and the first payment settles normally. Your UI doesn't show the second result as a failed payment, and your server charges once. Backgrounding. Open the sheet, go to the home screen, and return to the app. Repeat after switching to another app. startPayment settles exactly once, isProcessing returns to false, and the next tap opens a new sheet. If the next payment reports code: 'IN_PROGRESS', or the app stays in its processing state, open an issue with the platform and OS version. Then check the release configuration: iOS: the Merchant ID in your plugin config is the one whose Payment Processing Certificate is installed in your gateway, and your server uses the gateway's live keys. Android: googlePayEnvironment is 'PRODUCTION', since an omitted value means TEST. A release build that omits it logs googlePayEnvironment is not set once per app run, when the first payment starts. googlePayMerchantId is your Console merchant ID, the gateway values are your live ones, Google has approved the app, and the build is signed with your release key. Both: merchantName is the business name you want on the sheet.

This cookbook shows how to use @gmisoftware/react-native-pay for wallet payments and process them with Przelewy24 on your backend. The library is not a gateway SDK. It only presents the native payment sheet and returns the payment token that your backend maps to Przelewy24 APIs. It follows the same contract used across this library: the app collects PaymentResult and PaymentToken the backend maps the token to Przelewy24 API calls

Przelewy24 REST docs (Apple Pay): developers.przelewy24.pl Przelewy24 REST docs (Google Pay): developers.przelewy24.pl Przelewy24 payment integration docs entry point: developers.przelewy24.pl Przelewy24 mobile library docs (registration and verification concepts): GitHub README Use Przelewy24's official docs as the source of truth for provider request fields, signatures, endpoints, and enablement requirements.

Complete iOS (Apple Pay) setup: Apple Merchant ID Apple Pay capability enabled on your App ID Payment Processing Certificate Confirm your Przelewy24 account is configured for Apple Pay. Test on a real iOS device with Wallet configured.

Complete Android (Google Pay) setup: enableGooglePay: true (Expo plugin) Google Pay API enabled in Google Cloud gateway config in app code (googlePayMerchantId, googlePayEnvironment, googlePayGateway, googlePayGatewayMerchantId) Confirm your Przelewy24 account is configured for Google Pay. Test on a real device (or emulator with Google Play Services) and a wallet card.
Implement a backend endpoint that: accepts token payloads from app clients maps platform-specific token payloads to Przelewy24 fields verifies and persists payment status

App displays wallet button (ApplePayButton on iOS, GooglePayButton on Android). User confirms payment in the native sheet. App receives PaymentResult (status, token). App sends the token and order ID to backend over HTTPS. Backend looks up the order and calls Przelewy24 with its stored amount and platform-appropriate payload mapping. Backend verifies final status and returns checkout result to the app.

The server prices the order, and the sheet shows that amount. The token is charged inside onAuthorize, so on iOS the Apple Pay sheet waits for the charge and shows its outcome: import React, {useState} from 'react' import {ActivityIndicator, Platform, Text, View} from 'react-native' import { ApplePayButton, GooglePayButton, HybridPaymentHandler, createPaymentRequest, } from '@gmisoftware/react-native-pay' const API_URL = 'https://api.yourserver.com/payments/przelewy24' export function CheckoutWithPrzelewy24({ cartId, isSupported, }: { cartId: string isSupported: boolean // from HybridPaymentHandler.payServiceStatus() }) { const [isProcessing, setIsProcessing] = useState(false) const [error, setError] = useState<string | null>(null) const [isPaid, setIsPaid] = useState(false) const onPayPress = async () => { setIsProcessing(true) setError(null) try { // 1) Your server creates the order and computes its amount. For a cart // that already has an order, it returns that order, so a retry after a // lost response reuses the same order and idempotency key. const orderResponse = await fetch(`${API_URL}/orders`, { method: 'POST', headers: {'Content-Type': 'application/json'}, body: JSON.stringify({cartId}), }) if (!orderResponse.ok) { setError('Could not create the order. Please try again.') return } const order: { orderId: string amount: string currency: string status: 'pending' | 'paid' } = await orderResponse.json() if (order.status === 'paid') { // An earlier attempt was charged: show the confirmation, don't charge again. setIsPaid(true) return } // 2) The sheet shows the amount the server will charge. const request = createPaymentRequest({ amount: order.amount, label: 'Your Store', merchantName: 'Your Store', countryCode: 'PL', currencyCode: order.currency, // the currency the server charges googlePayMerchantId: 'your_google_pay_merchant_id', googlePayEnvironment: 'TEST', // switch to PRODUCTION for live traffic googlePayGateway: 'przelewy24', googlePayGatewayMerchantId: 'your_przelewy24_gateway_merchant_id', }) // 3) Charge the token on your server while the sheet waits. const result = await HybridPaymentHandler.startPayment(request, { onAuthorize: async (token) => { const response = await fetch(`${API_URL}/wallet`, { method: 'POST', headers: {'Content-Type': 'application/json'}, body: JSON.stringify({ platform: Platform.OS, // ios | android orderId: order.orderId, token, }), }) if (!response.ok) { const {error} = await response.json() return {status: 'failure', error} } return {status: 'success'} }, }) // result.status is 'success' only when your server reported the charge. // Show the order confirmation from your server's order status. if (result.status === 'success') { setIsPaid(true) } else if (result.status === 'failed') { // Includes a charge your server declined. On Android the Google Pay // sheet has already closed, so this is the only place the payer sees it. setError(result.error ?? 'The payment failed. Please try again.') } // 'cancelled': the payer closed the sheet, so show nothing. } catch { setError('Could not reach the server. Please try again.') } finally { setIsProcessing(false) } } if (isPaid) return <Text>Payment received. Thank you!</Text> if (!isSupported) return null if (isProcessing) return <ActivityIndicator /> return ( <View> {error ? <Text>{error}</Text> : null} {Platform.OS === 'ios' ? ( <ApplePayButton buttonType="buy" buttonStyle="black" onPress={onPayPress} style={{width: '100%', height: 48}} /> ) : ( <GooglePayButton buttonType="buy" theme="dark" radius={4} onPress={onPayPress} style={{width: '100%', height: 48}} /> )} </View> ) } The client's PaymentResult is not proof of payment: your server, and Przelewy24's notification to it, are the source of truth for the amount and the payment status. On Android, Google Pay closes its sheet before onAuthorize runs; see Charge before the sheet closes.

Forward at least: token.paymentData (opaque payload; token format is platform/provider-dependent) order identifier, which your backend uses to look up the amount and currency, and for idempotency optional platform marker (ios / android) to simplify provider mapping Don't send the amount from the client: the server takes it from the order. Do not parse or transform paymentData in the client beyond forwarding it.

Provider field mapping must remain server-side. Keep this as an internal adapter and follow Przelewy24 docs for exact request schemas. Retries must not charge twice. The client creates the order on every press, and a press can follow a charge whose response never arrived. So: /orders returns the cart's existing order, with its status, instead of creating another one. /wallet keys idempotency on the order ID and doesn't charge an order that is already paid. app.post('/payments/przelewy24/wallet', async (req, res) => { const {platform, token, orderId} = req.body // 1) Look up the order: the amount and currency come from it, never from the request. const order = await orders.findForUser(orderId, req.user.id) if (!order) return res.status(404).json({error: 'Order not found'}) if (order.status === 'paid') return res.json({success: true, providerPaymentId: order.providerPaymentId}) // 2) Branch mapping by wallet platform. // 3) Build Przelewy24 request with required signatures/merchant fields. // 4) Persist payment status and return result. const p24Result = await przelewy24Client.createWalletPayment({ wallet: platform === 'ios' ? 'APPLE_PAY' : 'GOOGLE_PAY', // Stored in the currency's minor unit (grosze for PLN), not multiplied here. amountMinor: order.amountMinor, currency: order.currency, orderId: order.id, // Not token.transactionIdentifier: it is missing on Android. idempotencyKey: `wallet-${order.id}`, walletTokenPayload: token?.paymentData, rawToken: token, }) res.json({success: true, providerPaymentId: p24Result.id}) })

Always use HTTPS between app and backend. Never log raw token payloads. Take amount and currency from the server-side order, never from the request; check order ownership. Use idempotency keys based on your order ID, not on token.transactionIdentifier. Treat provider callbacks/webhooks and verification as the source of final payment state.

This package does not include a native Przelewy24 SDK adapter; integration is done through your backend. For production mapping and validation rules, rely on Przelewy24's official Apple Pay and Google Pay documentation.

React Native Pay is a unified payment module for React Native that supports Apple Pay (iOS) and Google Pay (Android) through a single, type-safe API for presenting native payment sheets and returning payment tokens.

One hook — usePaymentCheckout() handles availability, cart, and payment flow. Native buttons — ApplePayButton and GooglePayButton for platform-correct UI. Unified API — Shared request/result model across platforms; button component remains platform-specific. TypeScript — Full types and IntelliSense for requests, results, and tokens. Expo — Config plugin for Apple Pay entitlements and Google Pay metadata. Nitro Modules — High-performance native bindings.

React Native apps (Expo or bare) that need Apple Pay and/or Google Pay. Teams that want a single integration instead of maintaining two separate SDKs. Apps that already use (or plan to use) a payment gateway (e.g. Stripe, Braintree) and need the payment token from the device to charge on the server.

Check availability — isSupported and hasActiveCard from usePaymentCheckout() or HybridPaymentHandler.payServiceStatus(). See Check availability. Build the cart — addItem() / addItems() (or build a PaymentRequest yourself). Show the button — ApplePayButton on iOS, GooglePayButton on Android. Start payment — startPayment(); user completes the sheet; you receive a token. Send token to server — Your backend uses the token with your payment gateway to complete the charge. The library does not process payments itself; it gives you the token and metadata so your server can.

Renders native payment buttons (ApplePayButton / GooglePayButton). Starts Apple Pay / Google Pay sheets and returns PaymentResult + token payload. Provides hook-based cart helpers (usePaymentCheckout) and low-level API (HybridPaymentHandler).
It does not charge cards by itself. It does not replace your gateway SDK/backend payment flow. It does not bypass Apple Developer / Google Pay onboarding and account setup.

Use Apple Pay and Google Pay only for physical goods and for services used outside the app, such as a delivery, a ride, a ticket or a donation to an approved nonprofit. On iOS, real-time person-to-person services are also allowed (see 3.1.3(d) below). Digital content and in-app features, such as subscriptions to digital content, premium content or unlocked features, must as a rule use the stores' own billing, with the exceptions below. A subscription to physical goods, such as a monthly delivery, may use Apple Pay and Google Pay. App Store: App Review Guideline 3.1.1 requires In-App Purchase to unlock features, subscriptions or premium content. Under 3.1.3(e), physical goods and services used outside the app must use other payment methods, such as Apple Pay. Under 3.1.3(d), real-time person-to-person services between two people, such as tutoring or a medical consultation, may also use other payment methods; one-to-few and one-to-many real-time services must use In-App Purchase. Google Play: the Payments policy requires Google Play Billing for digital goods and in-app features. In some regions, such as the United States and the European Economic Area, developers enrolled in one of Google's alternative billing programs may offer another billing system to users there; the Payments policy lists the programs. Google Pay is not such a system: the Google Pay setup page limits it to physical goods and services and sends apps that sell digital goods to Play Billing. An app that sells digital goods with this library can be rejected in App Review or removed from Google Play. Apps that use Apple Pay must also follow App Review Guideline 4.9: Show all material purchase information to the user before the sale. For recurring payments, such as a monthly delivery, disclose at least the length of the renewal term and that it continues until cancelled, what is provided during each period, the charges, and how to cancel.

This page focuses on runtime behavior and integration boundaries so you can make your checkout resilient.

The library does not charge the user directly. It opens the native wallet sheet, returns a tokenized payment payload, and lets your backend complete the charge with your gateway. At a minimum: App checks wallet availability (isSupported / payServiceStatus()). App builds a PaymentRequest from cart items. User confirms payment in the native sheet. App receives PaymentResult (status, code, token). Backend validates order context and charges through your provider.

sequenceDiagram actor User participant App participant NativeSheet participant Backend participant Gateway App->>App: Build paymentRequest from cart App->>NativeSheet: startPayment(paymentRequest) User->>NativeSheet: Confirm or cancel NativeSheet-->>App: PaymentResult(status, code, token) alt success with token App->>Backend: POST token + amount + currency + orderId Backend->>Backend: Validate order state and idempotency Backend->>Gateway: Create charge/intent using token Gateway-->>Backend: Authorized or failed Backend-->>App: Final checkout status else status cancelled App->>App: Stay on checkout, no error else status failed App->>App: Handle result.code end

With onAuthorize, your backend charges the token before startPayment resolves: on iOS while the Apple Pay sheet is still up, on Android after the Google Pay sheet has closed. The result below already reflects the charge, so don't send result.token to your backend again. Every result has a status. When it isn't 'success', code says why: status success code What to do 'success' true none Forward result.token to your backend, unless onAuthorize already charged it. Wait for your backend before marking the order paid. 'cancelled' false 'CANCELLED' The user closed the sheet. Leave the checkout as it was and don't show an error. 'failed' false any other code See the table below. Neither platform rejects the startPayment promise for these outcomes. error is a message for your logs, and it is also set on a cancel ('Payment cancelled by user'). Branch on status and code, not on the message. import type { PaymentResult } from '@gmisoftware/react-native-pay' function describeOutcome(result: PaymentResult): string | null { switch (result.status) { case 'success': return null case 'cancelled': return null // the user closed the sheet case 'failed': switch (result.code) { case 'IN_PROGRESS': return null // the payment already in flight will settle case 'NOT_AVAILABLE': return 'Apple Pay / Google Pay is not available. Choose another payment method.' case 'PROVIDER_ERROR': return 'The payment did not go through. Try again or choose another payment method.' default: return 'Something went wrong. Please try again later.' } } }

code Meaning Where it comes from What to do 'CANCELLED' The sheet closed before the user authorized. iOS: the sheet closed without an authorization. PassKit doesn't say why, so a sheet that closes by itself also reports a cancel. Debug builds log a warning when the sheet closes within 1 second of appearing (see Troubleshooting). Android: the sheet returned RESULT_CANCELED, also when the user dismisses Google's sign-in prompt, or a Google Pay error has CANCELED / ERROR_CODE_USER_CANCELLED. Nothing. Don't show an error. 'IN_PROGRESS' Another payment is still in flight. No sheet was shown. Both: startPayment called while a payment hasn't settled (see isPaymentInProgress()). Ignore it. The payment in flight settles normally. 'CONFIGURATION' The request or the app's setup is invalid. Retrying won't help. Both: an invalid amount, a negative total, a currencyCode or countryCode that isn't an upper-case ISO code, an unknown merchant capability, invalid shippingMethods, and supportedNetworks that is empty, has an unknown name or has no network the platform offers. iOS: no Apple Pay merchant ID, an unknown shippingType. Android: more than two decimal places, an unknown googlePayAllowedAuthMethods value, PRODUCTION without googlePayMerchantId, googlePayGateway or googlePayGatewayMerchantId, and a Google Pay error with DEVELOPER_ERROR, ERROR_CODE_INVALID_PARAMETERS, ERROR_CODE_MERCHANT_ACCOUNT_ERROR or ERROR_CODE_UNSUPPORTED_API_VERSION. Fix the request or the setup; error says what is wrong. Show the user a generic error. 'NOT_AVAILABLE' The device can't show the payment sheet right now. iOS: PassKit can't create the sheet, which Apple documents for a user who can't pay with any of the request's networks, or can't show it (see Troubleshooting). Android: no current activity, the Google Pay sheet fails to start, and a Google Pay error with SIGN_IN_REQUIRED, API_NOT_CONNECTED, ERROR_CODE_BUYER_ACCOUNT_ERROR or ERROR_CODE_AUTHENTICATION_FAILURE. Offer another payment method. Show the pay button only as Check availability describes, from isSupported and hasActiveCard. 'PROVIDER_ERROR' Apple Pay, Google Pay or your onAuthorize reported a failure. Both: onAuthorize resolved with 'failure', rejected, or didn't settle within 25 seconds. Android: any other Google Pay error, such as a network or internal error, and payment data that is missing or can't be read. Let the user retry or choose another payment method. After a timeout, your server may still have charged: reconcile the order. 'UNKNOWN' Anything else. iOS: an unexpected error while starting the payment. Android: an unexpected result code or exception, or a Google Pay error without a status. Show a generic error and log error. A Google Pay error arrives either from loadPaymentData or as the sheet's RESULT_ERROR; both are mapped the same way, and its status code is added to error, for example Payment error: <message> (status code 10).

startPayment() from usePaymentCheckout returns status: 'failed' with code: 'UNKNOWN' when an exception occurs, and sets error to a PaymentError with the same code. Handle this as an app/runtime failure path (show generic error + retry).

Calling startPayment() with no cart items returns status: 'failed' with code: 'CONFIGURATION', and sets a "Cart is empty" error with the same code. An invalid amount or a negative total also returns code: 'CONFIGURATION' and sets error, without opening the sheet. Gate the pay button on items.length > 0.

PaymentToken.paymentData is an opaque gateway payload and is platform/gateway-dependent: Apple Pay (iOS): Base64-encoded data from the Apple Pay token payload. Google Pay (Android): Tokenization payload from Google Pay (tokenizationData.token), whose schema depends on your configured gateway. Always send the entire token object (or exactly the fields your gateway asks for) to your backend. Avoid parsing or transforming token payloads in the client.

Your backend should: Validate order ownership, amount, and currency from server-side order data. Use an idempotency key derived from your order ID to prevent duplicate charges. Call gateway APIs with the provider-specific token mapping. Persist both wallet result and gateway result for audit/debug. Return a final, app-friendly checkout status.

iOS: Merchant ID and Payment Processing Certificate set up and installed in your gateway. Android: Google Pay API enabled; production gateway merchant ID and environment configured. Backend: Endpoint validates the token, amount, and context and uses the gateway SDK to create the charge. Security: Never log or expose raw token payloads; use HTTPS and secure storage for any sensitive data. Next: API: usePaymentCheckout or Server-side processing.

Use the hook and the platform-specific button. Your server creates the order and prices it; the screen shows its lines and pays for that order. Pass onAuthorize to charge the token on your server: startPayment() resolves with status: 'success' only when your server charged the payment. On iOS the Apple Pay sheet waits for your server and shows its answer; on Android, Google Pay closes its sheet before onAuthorize runs. import React, { useEffect } from 'react' import { usePaymentCheckout, ApplePayButton, GooglePayButton, formatAmount, } from '@gmisoftware/react-native-pay' import { Platform, View, Text, ActivityIndicator } from 'react-native' // An order your server created and priced, for example when the user opened // checkout. Use your own type. Render the screen with `key={order.id}`, so a // new order starts with an empty cart instead of the previous order's lines. type Order = { id: string lines: { label: string; amount: string }[] } function CheckoutScreen({ order }: { order: Order }) { const { // Payment availability isSupported, isCheckingStatus, // Cart items, total, addItems, clearItems, // Payment processing startPayment, isProcessing, error, } = usePaymentCheckout({ merchantName: 'Your Store', currencyCode: 'USD', countryCode: 'US', // Charge on your server. It charges the order's stored amount, not one // the app sends, and keys idempotency on the order ID, so a retry after // a timeout can't charge twice. onAuthorize: async (token) => { const response = await fetch('https://api.yourserver.com/process-payment', { method: 'POST', headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' }, // `total` is what the sheet showed: the server rejects the charge // if the order no longer matches it. body: JSON.stringify({ token, orderId: order.id, total: formatAmount(total, 'USD') }), }) return response.ok ? { status: 'success' } : { status: 'failure', error: 'Payment failed' } }, }) // The sheet shows the lines your server priced. startPayment() fails // for an empty cart, so fill it before the user taps pay. useEffect(() => { addItems(order.lines) return clearItems }, [order, addItems, clearItems]) const handlePay = async () => { const result = await startPayment() if (result.status === 'success') { // Your server charged the payment: show your confirmation here. } // 'failed': `error` is set, including when your server declined or // could not be reached. // 'cancelled': the user closed the sheet, and `error` stays null. } if (isCheckingStatus) { return <View><ActivityIndicator /></View> } if (!isSupported) { return <View><Text>Apple Pay / Google Pay is not available</Text></View> } return ( <View style={{ padding: 20 }}> {items.map((item, index) => ( <Text key={index}>{item.label}: ${formatAmount(item.amount)}</Text> ))} <Text style={{ fontSize: 20, marginVertical: 10 }}>Total: ${total.toFixed(2)}</Text> {error && <Text style={{ color: 'red' }}>Error: {error.message}</Text>} {isProcessing ? ( <ActivityIndicator size="large" /> ) : ( Platform.OS === 'ios' ? ( <ApplePayButton buttonType="buy" buttonStyle="black" onPress={handlePay} style={{ width: '100%', height: 48 }} /> ) : ( <GooglePayButton buttonType="buy" theme="dark" radius={4} onPress={handlePay} style={{ width: '100%', height: 48 }} /> ) )} </View> ) } Without onAuthorize, Apple Pay shows its success checkmark as soon as the user authorizes, and startPayment() resolves with status: 'success' before your server has charged anything. Don't tell the user the payment succeeded until your server answers. See Server-side processing for timeouts, retries and Android behavior. If the user builds the cart in the app, have your server create or update the order for that cart before the user taps pay, and keep the same order ID across retries so the idempotency key stays the same. See Dynamic cart. If you are integrating with Przelewy24, follow the provider cookbook: Przelewy24.

iOS: Real device with a card in Wallet; Simulator has limited support. Android: Real device or emulator with Google Play Services; add a card in Google Pay. For Google Pay, configure googlePayMerchantId, googlePayEnvironment, googlePayGateway, and googlePayGatewayMerchantId when you move to a real gateway (see Android setup and API: usePaymentCheckout).

react-native-nitro-modules and @gmisoftware/react-native-pay installed. Native config done (Expo plugin + prebuild, or bare iOS entitlements + Android manifest). Checkout screen uses usePaymentCheckout and the platform-specific button. Apple and/or Google account/platform configuration is complete. Backend endpoint validates order amount/currency and processes the token with your gateway. Idempotency and retry handling are implemented server-side. Real-device tests passed on iOS and Android. Configure your app and Google Pay for Android.

In app.json (or app.config.js), enable Google Pay: { "expo": { "plugins": [ ["@gmisoftware/react-native-pay", { "enableGooglePay": true }] ] } } Use the same plugin with merchantIdentifier if you also support iOS.
In Google Cloud Console, open your project. Enable the Google Pay API for the project. For production, Google must also approve your app in the Google Pay & Wallet Console. See Production access.

Google Pay needs a Google Pay merchant ID for production, plus your payment gateway details (Stripe, Braintree, etc.) and gateway merchant ID. Configure them in usePaymentCheckout (or in your PaymentRequest): import { usePaymentCheckout } from '@gmisoftware/react-native-pay' usePaymentCheckout({ merchantName: 'Your Store', // shown on the Google Pay sheet currencyCode: 'USD', countryCode: 'US', googlePayMerchantId: 'your_google_pay_merchant_id', googlePayEnvironment: 'TEST', // or 'PRODUCTION' googlePayGateway: 'stripe', // or braintree, square, adyen, etc. googlePayGatewayMerchantId: 'your_stripe_merchant_id', }) If you omit merchantName, the Google Pay sheet shows your app's label (android:label in the manifest). If you omit googlePayEnvironment, Google Pay runs in TEST, in release builds too. A release build that omits it logs a warning once per app run when a payment starts, through usePaymentCheckout, HybridPaymentHandler.startPayment or createPaymentRequest. An availability check, and the raw handler from getPaymentHandler(), log nothing. Set 'PRODUCTION' for live payments, or 'TEST' to keep the test environment without the warning. Supported gateways include: stripe, braintree, square, adyen, authorizenet, checkoutltd. See Google Pay Gateway Tokens for the full list and exact identifiers.
npx expo prebuild --clean npx expo run:android

Use a real device or an emulator with a Google Play system image, signed in to a Google account. In googlePayEnvironment: 'TEST', Google Pay shows its test cards, and no token can be used for a live charge. See TEST environment for what it can't verify and how to get a token your gateway accepts. PRODUCTION needs Google's approval. See Production access. Before each release, run the release checklist.

If the user switches to another app while the Google Pay sheet is open, Android can kill your app's process to free memory. When the user comes back and finishes or closes the sheet, your app restarts with a new JS runtime. The startPayment() call that opened the sheet no longer exists, so its result is dropped: No token reaches your app, so your backend charges nothing. The cart and checkout screen are gone unless your app restores them. The user has to start the payment again. The payment survives a recreated Activity, for example after a configuration change your Activity doesn't handle: the result still reaches startPayment(). To reproduce a process death, open the sheet, press Home, run adb shell am kill <your.package.name>, reopen the app from Recents, and close the sheet.

documents.t: By default, Google Pay accepts both kinds of card (googlePayAllowedAuthMethods): 'CRYPTOGRAM_3DS' cards are tokenized on the device. The token holds a 3-D Secure cryptogram. 'PAN_ONLY' cards are saved to the payer's Google account. The token holds the card number and no cryptogram, so the payment is not authenticated. Google requires you to trigger 3-D Secure (step-up authentication) for PAN_ONLY payments under the same rules as any other card payment. This matters most where Strong Customer Authentication applies, such as the EEA. Your gateway runs the 3-D Secure step after your backend receives the token; see your gateway's Google Pay guide. See Google's Android tutorial and integration checklist. If your gateway cannot run 3-D Secure for Google Pay, accept only device tokens: import { usePaymentCheckout } from '@gmisoftware/react-native-pay' usePaymentCheckout({ googlePayAllowedAuthMethods: ['CRYPTOGRAM_3DS'], }) Google can also report whether it has already verified the card and the cardholder (assuranceDetailsRequired), so you can skip the step-up when both checks pass. This library does not request it yet.
GooglePayButton with buttonType="donate" is only for nonprofits that Google has validated. See the Google Pay brand guidelines. Get Google's approval before you collect donations with Google Pay.

Button not showing: Ensure enableGooglePay: true is set, prebuild was run, and Google Play Services is available. Google Pay unavailable: Add a card in Google Pay on the device; for testing use googlePayEnvironment: 'TEST' and correct gateway config. See Troubleshooting for more. If you are integrating with Przelewy24, see Przelewy24 for an end-to-end app + backend flow.

Your app should contain: Entitlement key: com.apple.developer.in-app-payments with your merchant ID(s). Info.plist key: ReactNativePayApplePayMerchantIdentifiers with merchant ID(s). In app code, pass Google Pay config in usePaymentCheckout (or PaymentRequest): googlePayMerchantId googlePayEnvironment (TEST for sandbox, PRODUCTION for live). Omitted, it is TEST. A release build logs a warning once per app run when a payment starts, but not on an availability check. googlePayGateway googlePayGatewayMerchantId
Test on a real device or Play-enabled emulator. Ensure Google Play Services is available. Ensure at least one wallet card is configured in Google Pay.

The @gmisoftware/react-native-pay Expo config plugin configures native projects so Apple Pay and Google Pay work without manual edits.
Add the plugin to app.json or app.config.js: { "expo": { "plugins": [ [ "@gmisoftware/react-native-pay", { "merchantIdentifier": "merchant.com.yourcompany.app", "enableGooglePay": true } ] ] } }

Both options are optional. Listed without options ("plugins": ["@gmisoftware/react-native-pay"]), the plugin changes nothing. Option Type Description merchantIdentifier string or string[] Apple Pay Merchant ID(s). If omitted, Apple Pay entitlements are not added. Each ID should start with merchant.; prebuild warns when one does not. enableGooglePay boolean true adds the Google Pay metadata (com.google.android.gms.wallet.api.enabled) to the Android manifest. false removes it. If omitted, the manifest is left as it is, so an entry added by another plugin (Stripe, for example) stays. The plugin doesn't set the Google Pay environment. Pass googlePayEnvironment in app code; see Android (Google Pay).

iOS only (Apple Pay): ["@gmisoftware/react-native-pay", { "merchantIdentifier": "merchant.com.example.app" }] Android only (Google Pay): ["@gmisoftware/react-native-pay", { "enableGooglePay": true }] Both platforms: ["@gmisoftware/react-native-pay", { "merchantIdentifier": "merchant.com.example.app", "enableGooglePay": true }] Multiple Merchant IDs (iOS): ["@gmisoftware/react-native-pay", { "merchantIdentifier": ["merchant.com.example.app", "merchant.com.example.other"], "enableGooglePay": true }]

Install the payment library and its required dependency in your React Native (or Expo) app.

React Native 0.70 or newer (tested with 0.86 / Expo SDK 57) react-native-nitro-modules 0.36.0 or newer (required) Android minSdkVersion 26 or newer (required for Nitro Modules prefab) Expo 53–57, optional: only if you use Expo (SDK 57 requires Node.js 22.13+)
This package depends on Nitro. Install it first: npm install react-native-nitro-modules # or yarn add react-native-nitro-modules # or bun add react-native-nitro-modules
npm install @gmisoftware/react-native-pay # or yarn add @gmisoftware/react-native-pay # or bun add @gmisoftware/react-native-pay

Add the plugin in app.json or app.config.js so that: iOS: Apple Pay entitlements (Merchant ID) are set. Android: Google Pay is enabled in the manifest when you want it. See Expo plugin for the exact config, then: iOS (Apple Pay) for Apple Developer setup. Android (Google Pay) for Google Pay and gateway setup. Bare React Native setup for manual Xcode/AndroidManifest configuration.
After adding or changing the plugin: npx expo prebuild --clean Then run your app as usual (npx expo run:ios or npx expo run:android).

Configure your app and Apple Developer account for Apple Pay.

In app.json (or app.config.js), add the plugin with your Merchant ID: { "expo": { "plugins": [ ["@gmisoftware/react-native-pay", { "merchantIdentifier": "merchant.com.yourcompany.app" }] ] } } The plugin also writes the Merchant ID to the Info.plist key ReactNativePayApplePayMerchantIdentifiers, and the runtime API reads the first ID from there. You only need applePayMerchantIdentifier in code if you want to override it at runtime. Without either, the payment fails with code: 'CONFIGURATION' and an error starting "No Apple Pay merchant identifier configured".
Open Certificates, Identifiers & Profiles. Create a new Merchant ID (e.g. merchant.com.yourcompany.app). Note it exactly; it must match the plugin and your code.
In Identifiers, select your App ID. Enable Apple Pay Payment Processing. Associate the Merchant ID you created.
documents.s: Enable Apple Pay on your App ID

documents.t: In the Merchant ID page, create a Payment Processing Certificate. Follow Apple’s steps (CSR, etc.) and download the certificate. Install it in your payment processor (e.g. Stripe, Braintree) as per their docs. The library does not process payments; your gateway uses this certificate to validate tokens. If you are integrating with Przelewy24, see Przelewy24 for an end-to-end app + backend flow.

Apple Pay shows the total as "Pay merchant". Pass your business name as merchantName: import { usePaymentCheckout } from '@gmisoftware/react-native-pay' usePaymentCheckout({ merchantName: 'Your Store', currencyCode: 'USD', countryCode: 'US', }) The sheet lists your cart items and then the total line "Pay Your Store", which the library adds for you. If you omit merchantName, the total uses your app's display name (CFBundleDisplayName).

The iOS Simulator shows the Apple Pay sheet without a card, but its token can't be charged. See what the Simulator can't verify. On an iPhone, test with an Apple Pay sandbox tester and Apple's test cards. See Sandbox on an iPhone. Before each release, run the release checklist.

Button not showing: ApplePayButton renders on iOS whatever the setup, so check the availability result your app hides it on. Payment fails with CONFIGURATION: Ensure the Merchant ID matches exactly and is in the app after npx expo prebuild --clean. See Troubleshooting for more.
Common issues and fixes for React Native Pay.

Ensure your cart is not empty. startPayment() fails with code: 'CONFIGURATION' and a "Cart is empty" error when items.length === 0. Test on a real device whenever possible (simulator/emulator payment support is limited). Re-run native generation after plugin changes: npx expo prebuild --clean

startPayment doesn't throw for a declined, cancelled or misconfigured payment. It resolves with a PaymentResult whose status and code say how it ended; Error codes explains each code. When debugging: Read error: it names the problem, and on Android it ends with Google Pay's status code. Branch on code in your app, though: the text may change. A 'CANCELLED' you didn't cause by closing the sheet usually points to setup. See The Apple Pay sheet closes right away and Cancelled on a device without a Google account.

On React Native 0.80+ (e.g. Expo SDK 57), the app can abort at startup with a stack ending in folly::dynamic::get<bool>() / BaseViewProps. Linking the library is enough; no pay button needs to be on screen. Cause: NitroPay.podspec defined FOLLY_NO_CONFIG, mismatching React Native core's folly config. Fixed in 0.0.17 — upgrade, then rebuild: npx expo prebuild --clean
