documents.t: ApplePayButton renders on iOS whatever the Apple Pay setup, and renders nothing on Android. If it's missing on iOS, your app hid it: check what isSupported and hasActiveCard returned (see Check availability). On a device without Wallet set up, isSupported can be true while hasActiveCard is false.

Merchant ID mismatch: The Expo plugin merchantIdentifier must exactly match your Apple Developer Merchant ID. Missing capability: Confirm "Apple Pay Payment Processing" is enabled in Xcode and linked to the same Merchant ID. No merchant ID in the app: code: 'CONFIGURATION' with an error starting "No Apple Pay merchant identifier configured" means neither applePayMerchantIdentifier nor the Info.plist key ReactNativePayApplePayMerchantIdentifiers is set. The Expo plugin writes the key; in a bare app, see Bare React Native. Add a valid card in Settings -> Wallet & Apple Pay. Confirm the App ID has Apple Pay enabled and linked to your Merchant ID. For production, ensure your Payment Processing Certificate is created and installed in your gateway.
documents.s: The Apple Pay sheet doesn't open or the payment fails

documents.t: startPayment resolves with status: 'cancelled' whenever the sheet closes before the user authorizes. PassKit doesn't tell the app why the sheet closed, so a sheet that closes by itself, or barely appears, reports the same cancel. One reported cause is a merchant ID that Apple Pay isn't set up for: The merchant ID in the request, or the first one in the Info.plist key ReactNativePayApplePayMerchantIdentifiers, must be listed under the Apple Pay Payment Processing capability in Xcode and in your App ID. Rebuild after changing the Expo plugin's merchantIdentifier: npx expo prebuild --clean. In a debug build, the library logs a warning when the sheet closes less than 1 second after it appeared, before the user authorized. The result is still status: 'cancelled' and code: 'CANCELLED', and a user who closes the sheet that fast gets the same warning. The warning starts with [NitroPay] The Apple Pay sheet closed and appears in the Xcode console, not in Metro. Without Xcode, stream the simulator's log: xcrun simctl spawn booted log stream --predicate 'eventMessage CONTAINS "[NitroPay]"' On a physical device, open Console.app on the Mac, select the device and search for [NitroPay]. Release builds log nothing, because the payment request holds your merchant IDs, item labels and amounts. See Apple Pay button not showing for the full checklist.
documents.s: The Apple Pay sheet closes right away

documents.t: startPayment resolves with status: 'failed', code: 'NOT_AVAILABLE' and this error when PassKit could not show the Apple Pay sheet. No sheet appeared and nothing was charged. The payment has ended, so the next startPayment call opens a new sheet. If you see it while the app is in the foreground, open an issue with the iOS version and what was on screen.

The payment fails with code: 'CONFIGURATION' and Unknown merchant capability "<value>". Use "3DS", "EMV", "Credit" or "Debit" when merchantCapabilities contains any other value, on Android too. Case doesn't matter ('3ds' works). See MerchantCapability.

Use only supported Apple button values: buttonType: 'buy' | 'setUp' | 'book' | 'donate' | 'continue' | 'reload' | 'addMoney' | 'topUp' | 'order' | 'rent' | 'support' | 'contribute' | 'tip' buttonStyle: 'white' | 'whiteOutline' | 'black'

GooglePayButton renders on Android whatever the Google Pay setup, and renders nothing on iOS. If it's missing on Android, your app hid it: check what isSupported and hasActiveCard returned (see Check availability).

Set enableGooglePay: true in your Expo plugin config. Ensure Google Play Services is available (real device or Play-enabled emulator). Add at least one card in Google Pay on the device. Use googlePayEnvironment: 'TEST' for test flows. Verify googlePayMerchantId, googlePayGateway, and googlePayGatewayMerchantId.
documents.s: isSupported or hasActiveCard is false on Android

documents.t: The check asked the Google Pay TEST environment, which reports a card whether or not there is one. Pass googlePayEnvironment: 'PRODUCTION' to usePaymentCheckout or payServiceStatus. An emulator with no Google account signed in reports false even in TEST. See Check availability.
documents.s: hasActiveCard is true without a card

documents.t: Google Pay asks the user to sign in to a Google account before it shows the sheet. Dismissing that prompt returns the same result as closing the sheet, so startPayment resolves with status: 'cancelled'. Sign in to a Google account on the device or emulator, and add a card to it.
documents.s: Cancelled on a device without a Google account

documents.t: When Google Pay reports a setup problem, such as DEVELOPER_ERROR, the result has code: 'CONFIGURATION' and Google's status code at the end of error (for example (status code 10)). Google logs the details of merchant setup problems to logcat: adb logcat -s WalletMerchantError The OR_BIBED_* codes there are explained on Google's troubleshooting page, such as OR_BIBED_06 for the example gateway in production.
Run npx expo prebuild --clean and rebuild. Ensure no other plugin overrides Google Pay metadata in AndroidManifest.xml.

The library writes to logcat in debug builds only. Release builds log nothing, because the payment request holds your merchant IDs, item labels and amounts. To see the logs, run a debug build and filter by tag: adb logcat -s HybridPaymentHandler HybridGooglePayButton Payment errors don't depend on logs: they reach your app in result.error.

ApplePayButton and GooglePayButton take a plain function as onPress. Earlier versions required wrapping it with callback() from react-native-nitro-modules. That is no longer needed: remove the wrapper, and the callback import if nothing else uses it. import { Platform } from 'react-native' import { ApplePayButton, GooglePayButton } from '@gmisoftware/react-native-pay' const handlePay = async () => { // Call startPayment() from usePaymentCheckout here } {Platform.OS === 'ios' ? ( <ApplePayButton buttonType="buy" buttonStyle="black" onPress={handlePay} /> ) : ( <GooglePayButton buttonType="buy" theme="dark" onPress={handlePay} /> )} A wrapped onPress still works, but TypeScript reports Type 'NitroViewWrappedCallback<...>' is not assignable to type '() => void', and development builds log a warning.

If an app throws React Native Pay: the native PaymentHandler is not available, the app runs without the native module: Install react-native-nitro-modules (required): bun add react-native-nitro-modules. Rebuild after adding/upgrading the package. With Expo, run npx expo prebuild and use a development build: Expo Go doesn't include the native module. On web there is no native module. Importing the package works there, usePaymentCheckout reports isSupported: false, and both pay buttons render nothing.
documents.s: Nitro or native module not found

documents.t: Importing the package doesn't need the native module, so tests of code that only uses helpers such as formatAmount run without a mock. Tests that call HybridPaymentHandler, run a payment through usePaymentCheckout, or render a pay button on its platform need a mock of react-native-nitro-modules: jest.mock('react-native-nitro-modules', () => ({ NitroModules: { createHybridObject: () => ({ payServiceStatus: async () => ({ isSupported: true, hasActiveCard: true }), isPaymentInProgress: () => false, startPayment: async () => ({ status: 'success', success: true }), openPaymentSetup: () => {}, }), }, getHostComponent: (name: string) => name, callback: (func: unknown) => ({ f: func }), }))
If native build artifacts are stale: rm -rf node_modules ios/Pods ios/build android/build android/app/build bun install cd ios && pod install Then rebuild the app.
